result.summary: Followup 48 is real on the engine. Before the fix, in the plain store and under a cipher, the state played out like this: a drain's slot B with its fdatasync owed, then the next publish into B killed part way so the cache holds B torn. The reopen takes A, sweeps the owed publish's segment and acknowledges commits. After a power cut with the device holding B's owed record whole, the next open refuses: "the manifest slot manifest names pcs-...sup, which is missing from the directory". Fix: Db::open now opens both slot files without creating them (vault::open_slot_found; an absent file is passed over) and fdatasyncs each through a recorded call (vault::sync_slot, which writes a "sync_slot" trace record). This happens in the block before open_refusals, so both syncs come before anything is removed or written. Either sync's failure is the open's answer. New seam: Options::fail_open_other_slot_sync, which names the inode it failed for. The taken slot is now opened read-only instead of with vault::open_slot, at the same syscall count. The "open_slot" trace records the real path, so a cipher store's slots can be filtered by their directory. Tests: the torn-over-owed power-cut test, plain and cipher, which also holds the seam's refusal leaving the directory as found; an absent-other-slot test, plain and cipher, on a rename-shape store. an_open_makes_the_slot_it_takes_durable is restated: both slots must be on the device by page flags, and a check that reads the call record runs without root (followup 28). The pending-adoption tests now also require both slots' syncs before the slot write. The full suite is green with --no-fail-fast, and lint and fmt are green. 13 mutants were run: 10 killed. M3 (sync placed after open_refusals but before the sweep) survives as expected, because open_refusals removes nothing; the fix is at the stricter place. M12 (sync order swapped) is equivalent. M13 (continue changed to break) only differs where the slot just read has vanished, which nothing can reach.
result.shape_landed: Db::open makes both manifest slots durable as the page cache holds them, before open_refusals and so before any removal or slot write. For each of the taken slot and the other one: vault::open_slot_found (File::open on the real path, no create, NotFound -> None, passed over), then vault::sync_slot (fdatasync, recorded in the trace after it returns). A failure, or the test seam (fail_open_slot_sync for the taken slot, the new fail_open_other_slot_sync for the other, each naming the inode), is the open's error with nothing changed. The other slot is synced whatever it read as: torn, older, or newer and skipped for pending segments.
result.success_path_cost: Only at Db::open. Where the other slot file exists: one more open(2), one fdatasync of a file that is normally clean, and one close(2). Where it is absent (a rename-shape store): one failed open(2). The taken slot's existing open/fdatasync/close now uses a read-only open, same count. Nothing on commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish or read paths.

result.summary:
Followup 48, repair round 1. The defect is real and I built it on the engine, for a plain store and under a cipher. Here is the sequence: a drain publishes slot B with its fdatasync still owed. The next publish into B is killed part way through, so the page cache holds B torn. The reopen takes A, fdatasyncs A, sweeps the owed publish's segment and acknowledges commits. Then a power cut, with the device's B still holding the owed publish whole. The next open refuses: "the manifest slot manifest names pcs-...sup, which is missing from the directory" (before.log).

The fix: Db::open opens both slot files without creating them (vault::open_slot_found; a file that is not there is passed over) and fdatasyncs both through vault::sync_slot, before open_refusals and before any removal or write. Either sync failing is the open's answer, with every file left as it was found. The new seam is Options::fail_open_other_slot_sync, and its error names the inode.

This round's repairs:
(1) Both seams' errors are now passed into vault::sync_slot and take the place of the fdatasync's result there. A failed sync is therefore never recorded. A record made before the sync (E2) or a seam answered after a sync that ran (E3) now records a failure, and the test refuses that.
(2) The torn test now checks the record of the failing open: it must hold the taken slot's sync and not the failed one's.
(3) The torn test now requires that the first slot write after the reopen (the flush's publish) comes after both slots' syncs, matched by the real path. This makes a cipher test read an open_slot record, which kills E4. The check sits after the power-cut check, so on the unfixed engine the first failure is still the refusal (E7c).
(4) CLAUDE.md's entry now says the seam stands in for the call's result.

Extra mutants: E2, E3, E4, E7a and E8 are killed. E5 is killed as root by the page-flag tests and survives an unprivileged run (setpriv uid 65534, 189 passed), as expected.

E1/E6 survives, and I held it by reading rather than by a test. manifest_read_all opens both slot files earlier in the same open and already returns every error except NotFound. So open_slot_found's other errors can only happen if the file changes between two opens in one call, or if the process runs out of file descriptors.

E7b shows the failing-first evidence depends on the recorded device image. With the cut slot always torn and the second sync removed, the torn test passes the power-cut check and fails only at the sync-record assertions.

Final runs: durable 189 passed, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5, lib 404; lint and fmt green.
result.shape_landed: At Db::open, in the block that ends "slot.landed(m.slot); synced[m.slot] = m.seq;" and ahead of open_refusals, the open runs a loop over the taken slot and the other slot. Each file is opened read-only with vault::open_slot_found, which never creates a file; one that is not there is skipped. Each is then fdatasynced through vault::sync_slot(f, path, failed). sync_slot records the sync in the I/O trace (by the file's real path) only once it has returned. Its `failed` argument is a test seam's error and stands in for the fdatasync's result (fail_open_slot_sync for the taken slot, fail_open_other_slot_sync for the other). The open_slot trace record now uses the real path. Under the rename shape the other slot is usually absent and is skipped. A manifest.alt left over from a slots life would be synced (not changed this round).
result.success_path_cost: Db::open only. Where the other slot file exists: one open(2), one fdatasync of a file that usually has nothing dirty, and one close(2). Where it does not exist (a rename-shape store): one open(2) that fails with ENOENT. The taken slot's sync is the same fdatasync as before, now opened read-only instead of read-write+create, so it costs the same syscalls. In the success path the seam costs one bool test per slot at open. Nothing changes on commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish or read. Not timed here; open-cost times the open later in this run.

nonblocking: Success-path cost, by function: Db::open (src/db.rs ~28817-28851) now opens the taken slot read-only with File::open where it used to call vault::open_slot (O_WRONLY|O_CREAT). The syscall count is the same: one open, one fdatasync, one close. For the other slot it adds one open(2), one fdatasync and one close(2) where the file exists, and an open(2) failing with ENOENT where it does not. Both seams cost one bool test each. vault::open_slot_found calls real(), a locate() over the vault registry, which is the same lookup open_slot made before. open_slot's trace now computes real(path), but only behind IO_TRACE_ON, so it is free when unset. No other path changes: commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish and read are untouched. This is within what the brief allows.

Rename shape (manifest_slots off): the brief says 'one manifest and nothing to add', but the loop still runs there. It costs one ENOENT open(2) of manifest.alt at each open, and it fdatasyncs a stale manifest.alt left over from a slots life. Both are harmless and open-only. Followup 48, repair round 2. I confirmed the defect on the engine before fixing it, plain and under a cipher (before.log). The state: a drain's slot B is written with its fdatasync owed; the next publish into B is killed part way, so the page cache holds B torn; the reopen takes A, syncs only A, sweeps the owed publish's segment and acknowledges commits. A power cut then leaves the device's copy of B as the owed record whole, and every later open refuses with "the manifest slot manifest names pcs-...sup, which is missing from the directory". The fix (unchanged this round): Db::open opens each slot file it finds without making one (vault::open_slot_found) and fdatasyncs the taken slot and the other through vault::sync_slot, which records the sync only once it has returned. Both syncs run before open_refusals and before anything is removed or written. Either sync's failure is the open's answer. The seam Options::fail_open_other_slot_sync names the inode it failed for.

This round's changes. The reviewers expected R1 (skip the other slot's sync when the newest slot was passed over for pending segments) to be equivalent. It is not. The open writes over that skipped slot only after its sweep, so a kill between the two leaves the device holding an earlier owed publish that names a segment the sweep removed. I added a test section for it (plain only; osl_skipped and osl_pending_of in tests/durable.rs). It forges the pending slot, loses one of its segments, and uses tear_open_slot_write to stop the open between sweep and slot write; R1 now fails it with the "missing from the directory" refusal. R2 cannot be built as stated, because no Option holds landings at open. Instead, 40 runs of the torn tests, four at a time beside the whole durable binary, never fired a premise assert. R3, R6 and R7 are killed; R4 is equivalent like M3, and R5 is a cost mutant no test can see. I also added one clause to CLAUDE.md about the skipped slot. Nothing under src/ changed this round. Neighbour suites green: durable 189, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5, lib 404; lint and fmt are green.

Both syncs go through vault::sync_slot (an fdatasync that records "sync_slot" with the file's real path once it returns). A failure is the open's answer, with every file left as found. result.summary:
I built crash states under the rename shape (`manifest_slots` off) for (a) through (f) and ran them before any fix (before.log). Three real holes showed up, each in the clear, and the first two also under a cipher. (b) Followup 18: a seal whose publish failed its directory fsync after the rename was counted out with the seal queue still running. The next landing's fsync then named the segments durable and retired the log, and a power cut left a store that refused to open ("names seg-...sup, which is missing"). (c) Followup 32: an open of a manifest that a kill left renamed but not fsynced swept the old partitions with no directory fsync, so a power cut that kept the removals and lost the rename was refused. (d) Followup 55: a store written under `manifest_pending` and reopened in the rename shape took its pending names without fsyncing them. The next flush named them durable and retired the log, and a power cut that tore the segment failed with "key index checksum mismatch". Under a cipher the envelope is synced before the pending slot, and a test holds that.

The fixes, all on the arm's own path:
- `land_front` now stops the seal queue when `land_durable` fails under the rename shape, before the seal is counted out. The success path's one branch replaces the old `out?`.
- `Db::open`, under the rename shape when a manifest was read, now fsyncs any pending segments it took (with their ordered indexes under `ord_durable`, in the clear) and then the directory once, before the cipher sweep and before every removal. `Db::sync_pending` is factored out of the slots branch, which makes the same calls as before.

Guards, which passed before any fix and each have a mutant that fails them:
- (a) every step of a publish. Two follow-up mutants first survived because tests were missing; I added the tests and both are now killed.
- (e) a change of shape in both directions.
- (f) the refusal words name the file that was read (followup 58: `m.slot` is that file).

Mutants: 14 of my own, 13 killed. M3 survives: moving the stop after the count-out. I argued it is not observable, because the failed seal's table was already retired at its readable landing. After the fix the whole suite is green with `--no-fail-fast` (20 test binaries, 208 in `durable`), and lint and fmt pass. The work is uncommitted.
result.shape_landed: The rename shape only. In `Maint::land_front`, on `land_durable`'s Err under `!manifest_slots`, `stop_seals(&e)` runs before `in_seal` is decremented (Err branch only). In `Db::open`, under `!opts.manifest_slots && had_manifest`, before the cipher vault sweep and every removal: `Db::sync_pending(dir, &opts, &pending, &mut open_synced)` where pending names were taken in the clear, then the `fail_open_dir_sync` seam, then `vault::sync_dir(dir)`. Seams: `Options::fail_open_dir_sync`. Under the rename shape `fail_next_seal_dir_sync` fails the publish's directory fsync after its rename, and `watch_slot_writes` is called between a rename publish's rename and its directory fsync (`manifest_write` gained `fail_dir` and `watch` args). The slots path is unchanged apart from calling the factored `Db::sync_pending`, which makes the same calls.
result.success_path_cost: Store under the slots (the default): none. In `land_front` the new code is on the Err branch, and the success path's one branch replaces the `out?`. Rename shape (the arm): at every open that read a manifest, one directory fsync before anything is removed, plus one fsync per pending segment (and its index under `ord_durable`) only where a pending name was taken. At every rename publish, two relaxed loads and branches for the test seams (`fail_seal_dir_sync`, `slot_watching`) plus an `if let Some` in `manifest_write`. Not priced, per the brief.

blocking.title: Followup 36 is reported closed while a reachable crossing state the unit found is still open and recorded nowhere
blocking.detail: notes.md ('Followups closed: 18, 32, 36, 55, 58') closes 36. The unit's own not_built list names a crash state that can happen: a store goes slots -> rename -> slots, so manifest.alt is left over from its slots life. It is killed between a rename publish's rename and that publish's directory fsync, then reopened under the slots. That open fdatasyncs both slot files. It makes no directory fsync, because manifest_make_slots (src/db.rs:12566) fsyncs the directory only when it creates a slot file, and both already exist. It then sweeps what the renamed manifest stopped naming. Under the unit's own (c) model (the removals kept, the rename lost) a power cut leaves a store that refuses to open. This is exactly the 'crash across a change of shape' that brief item (e) asks for. The unit said in its result why it did not build the state, but it did not mark 36 open, did not put the window in ROADMAP.md or the follow-up list, and the JSON result never says which followups are closed (the brief requires that). The tidy units after this one would skip 36 on the strength of notes.md. blocking.title: Two seam loads and branches added to the rename shape's manifest publish success path, not folded into an existing check
blocking.detail: Maint::publish's rename branch now runs two relaxed atomic loads and branches on every publish: fail_seal_dir_sync, and slot_watching (.then_some). It also builds a closure and passes two more arguments into manifest_write, which branches on `if let Some(w) = watch` and `if fail_dir`. The brief allows the arm only the open's one directory fsync and, for a store with pending names, the pending fsyncs. Rule 1 forbids anything else on a manifest publish's success path beyond a load and a branch folded into a check the path already makes, and the rename branch had no such check before. The implementer's own success_path_cost lists these loads. Repair by folding both seams into a check the path already makes. vault::sync_dir already loads IO_TRACE_ON after every directory fsync, so a 'fail the next sync_dir' bit and the watch hook can ride that word, called before the sync, which also puts the watch between the rename and the fsync. The alternative is a single test-seam word whose one load replaces an existing branch. Keep (b) and the M9/M14b kills.

The open's added work under the rename shape is within the brief: sync_pending only where a pending name was taken in the clear, then one vault::sync_dir and an open_synced.push("."), a String allocation into a record the slots open keeps already. It runs at every open that read a manifest, even when nothing will be removed. The brief allows that, but the docs could say 'at every open' plainly. The slots branch's call to the factored Db::sync_pending makes the same calls in the same order as the inlined loop it replaces (diff read).

M3 (the stop moved after the count-out) survives. The land_front doc says 'a failure stops the queue before it is [counted out]', so the order is a documented contract with no test. The argument that it cannot be observed covers the frozen table only. A writer that reads in_seal==0 between the count-out and the stop (seals_first_partition, Db::in_flight) is not addressed, though join_seal itself propagates the Err. Either a seam that holds the window or a sentence that says why no decision reachable there matters.

blocking.title: Followup 36 is reported closed while a crash across a change of shape is still open and not built
blocking.detail: (e) asks for a crash across a change of shape in both directions. The implementer's own not_built list names a state a crash can leave: a store run under the slots (so manifest.alt exists), reopened under the rename shape, and killed between a rename publish's rename and its directory fsync. That store is then opened under the slots. The slots open fdatasyncs the two slot files' data and not the rename's directory entry. manifest_make_slots finds both files and makes no directory fsync (it fsyncs only `if made`). The open then removes what the new manifest stopped naming: a merge's inputs in the clear, and under a cipher the vault sweep. Under the unit's own model (removals kept, the earlier process's rename lost) that open is refused over acknowledged writes. This is the window (c) closes, reached through the other shape's open. The rename->slots test passes only because a store created under the rename shape has no manifest.alt, so manifest_make_slots does make the file and fsyncs the directory. Followup 36 is therefore not closed. The result must not list it as closed, or the tidy units skip it. Either build the state and fix it on a path the brief allows (for example the rename-shape open dealing with a leftover manifest.alt, if the owner accepts that as the arm's path), or report 36 as open and name this exact state (the case and its fix touch the slots open, which is outside this unit's allowance). Rule 9 then wants a ROADMAP item for it, since no item exists.

On the arm, every rename publish gains two relaxed loads and branches for test seams (fail_seal_dir_sync and slot_watching in Maint::publish, src/db.rs ~41346-41363). The cost is the same kind of seam load the slots path already pays in land_readable and watch_slot (rule 5, free when unset), but it is an addition to the arm's success path that the result should state as such. It does state it.

Only SyncPolicy::Always was run. The rename shape under EveryN (a buffered flush, a drain) was not built. By reading, `defer` in land_front is gated to the slots, so the rename shape takes the same publish, but nothing holds that.

A merge's or tier's rename publish that fails its directory fsync does not stop the queue. By reading this is sound: compact_run and the tier job each run vault::sync_dir on their outputs (src/db.rs ~13727, ~13895), apply_promotion fsyncs the directory before its publish (~41141), and inputs are retired only after publish() returns. result.summary:
Under the rename shape (Options::manifest_slots off), crash states were built and tested, and four holes were fixed on the arm's own path.
(b) followup 18: a seal whose rename publish fails now stops the seal queue in land_front, whether the failure comes after the rename or before it.
(c) followup 32: the rename open fsyncs the directory before it removes anything.
(d) followup 55: the rename open fsyncs any pending names it takes first.
(e) followup 36, this round's blocker: a store that ran slots -> rename -> slots and was killed in its rename life between a rename and its directory fsync could be refused after a power cut. This was shown failing first in before-r1.log: all four srs tests failed, each with "4 of 8 states lost ... the manifest slot manifest names par-..., which is missing".
- The fix: the rename open, after its directory fsync and before any removal, removes the manifest.alt a slots life left. Where manifest.alt held the manifest it read, it first writes that manifest as `manifest` (durable).
- So the next slots open finds a slot file missing and fsyncs the directory in manifest_make_slots.
- The slots open now calls manifest_make_slots before the cipher's envelope sweep. Before this, under a cipher, the sweep removed envelopes before that fsync. A crossing test fails make_slots's fsync through the extended fail_open_dir_sync seam: it failed with the old order under a cipher and passes now.
Blocker 3 (seam loads on the publish path): both seams now ride the word vault::sync_dir already loads. IO_TRACE_ON became IO_SEAMS with a hook bit; sync_dir_as(dir, kind) uses a cold sync_dir_seamed, and the hook is registered by Db::fail_next_seal_dir_sync / watch_slot_writes and held through a Weak. Maint::publish's rename branch is back to its base shape; manifest_write passes only a constant DirSync::Publish.
Round-1 tests added:
- The four srs crossing tests.
- A kill at the rename open of a store whose newest slot was alt.
- The crossing slots open whose directory fsync fails.
- A publish that fails before its rename (temp name taken by a directory) stops the queue.
- Under the slots, a seal's publish whose slot sync fails is written again by the next publish.
- (d) reopened without manifest_pending.
Each test is plain and under a cipher. The whole checked suite is green (durable 226), lint and fmt are green.
Followups closed: 18, 32, 36, 55, 58. Two exceptions: 36's sub-note about a v2 fixture comment in a_store_from_before_the_pending_flags_ was not touched. 58 rests on round 0's guard: the refusal names the slot file read (killed M11), and this round did not change it.
result.shape_landed:
Rename shape only, plus one reorder on the slots open:
- land_front: on land_durable's Err, under the rename shape, stop_seals before the count-out. This is the cold Err branch.
- Db::open, rename shape with a manifest read, before the cipher sweep and every removal, in this order:
  - Db::sync_pending for the pending names taken, in the clear.
  - One vault::sync_dir.
  - If manifest.alt was found by the existing slot-sync loop: where it was the slot taken, write `manifest` via slot.write_shape (temp, fsync, rename, directory fsync); then remove manifest.alt.
- Slots open: manifest_make_slots(dir, opts.fail_open_dir_sync) moved ahead of the vault sweep. It makes and fsyncs only where a slot file is missing, which is a crossing.
- Seams:
  - Options::fail_open_dir_sync (rename open's fsync; under the slots, make_slots's fsync).
  - vault::hook_dir_sync / DirSync / sync_dir_as, carrying Db::fail_next_seal_dir_sync's failure and watch_slot_writes's watch for rename publishes.
  - All of them ride the IO_SEAMS word that sync_dir already loaded.
result.success_path_cost:
Slots store: nothing added.
- land_front adds only the Err branch.
- manifest_make_slots's move ahead of the cipher sweep makes the same calls as before; under the slots it makes and fsyncs nothing unless a slot file is missing.
- vault::sync_dir_as makes the one load and branch that sync_dir made before. The load now comes before the fsync instead of after, and the rest is in a cold function.
- open_slot, sync_slot and sync_file now test a bit of the same word instead of a bool.
Rename shape:
- Manifest publish: nothing added. Maint::publish and manifest_write match the base, except that the DirSync::Publish constant is passed to sync_dir_as.
- Open, when nothing fails: one directory fsync before removals.
- Open where pending names were taken: their fsyncs (and their ordered indexes under ord_durable).
- Open where manifest.alt exists (a crossing only): an unlink. Where manifest.alt held the store, also one rename-shape manifest write (temp write, fsync, rename, directory fsync).
Not priced (per the brief).

result.cipher:
Every round-1 test runs under Encryption::Cipher as well (tests/durable.rs under_cipher()). Under a cipher the slot files and manifest.tmp go straight to the directory (vault::passes), so removing manifest.alt, the temp-name failure (a directory at manifest.tmp) and the crossing tests all apply as they do in the clear. Two cases are cipher-only, and both hold under a cipher now:
- Moving manifest_make_slots ahead of the vault sweep matters only under a cipher, because there the envelope sweep ran before that fsync. a_crossing_slots_open_..._under_a_cipher failed with the old order and passes.
- The (d) pending fsyncs stay skipped under a cipher (held.is_some()), since a pending envelope was synced before its slot; X4 shows this.
contract_changes: Under the rename shape, an open that finds manifest.alt removes it after its directory fsync. Where manifest.alt held the newest manifest, the open first writes that manifest as `manifest`.
The slots open makes a missing slot file and fsyncs the directory before the cipher's envelope sweep (it ran after the sweep before).
Options::fail_open_dir_sync also fails manifest_make_slots's directory fsync under the slots (test seam).
The rename-shape seams (Db::fail_next_seal_dir_sync, Db::watch_slot_writes) work through vault::hook_dir_sync, and IO_TRACE_ON became IO_SEAMS (trace and hook bits). Neither is public API.

Docs: Options::manifest_slots, Db::open, manifest_make_slots and fail_open_dir_sync say what is true now. CLAUDE.md's crash-discipline sentence on the rename shape covers removing the slots' file. Its 'A path only one arm exercises' amendment now names the fourth hole (the crossing back) and the rule about seams riding a word the path already loads. ROADMAP.md was not changed: no item existed, and 36 is closed.
not_verified: No real power cut or device fault. The states are copies edited by the model.
Whether ext4's journal already orders the earlier process's rename before the open's unlinks: the fix does not rely on it, and it was not checked.
The wasm group was not run. vault.rs is not built for wasm, and nothing in web/ was touched.
No timing was measured (brief: not priced).

nonblocking: src/db.rs ~29060 (slots open): moving manifest_make_slots ahead of the cipher's vault sweep does change the slots open's order. It only matters where a slot file is missing, i.e. a crossing back from the rename shape, and that is the defect (e) found, so it is within the arm's crossing. Still, the brief said nothing under the slots changes, so the commit message should say this reorder happens, and when.

src/db.rs Maint::land_front ~40047: only a seal's land_durable failure stops the queue under the rename shape. By reading, I checked that a merge's, tier's or promotion's failed rename publish needs no stop. compact_run/tier_run fsync their outputs' directory before they return (src/db.rs:13731, 13899), apply_promotion fsyncs before publish (41220), and their inputs are retired only after publish returns Ok. So a later publish names entries that are already durable, and the inputs it leaves are swept as orphans. That argument belongs in a comment next to the stop, or in the notes. It is not tested.

src/db/vault.rs DIR_HOOKS: the hook registry is process-wide. Once any test sets a hook, every sync_dir in the process takes the cold path, which takes a mutex and makes a liveness call on each hook, until the hook's store drops. This is harmless in tests, but the doc of hook_dir_sync could say it.

src/db.rs hook_publish_dir_sync: the hook upgrades the Weak<Shared> outside the hooks' lock. I believe it cannot be the last strong reference on the segment work's thread, because Maint holds an Arc<Shared>. I did not verify this for the inline segment work, where the publish runs on the writer's thread inside a Db method, which also holds the Arc.

CLAUDE.md amendment counts holes ('three holes', 'A fourth'). These are counts within a narrative of the change and not standing figures, but rule 9's 'no counts that move' could be read against them. Wording only.
extra_mutants: In land_front's Err branch, call stop_seals after in_seal.fetch_sub instead of before (round 0's M3, restated on the round-1 tree). The implementer argues it cannot be observed. Rerun it to confirm it still survives only for that reason.

In the rename open, with alt_found and taken == Some(MANIFEST_SLOTS[1]), write `manifest` with mseq (not mseq+1). Expected killer: a_store_moved_from_the_alt_slot_killed_at_its_rename_open_is_whole (an equal sequence makes the choice between the two files ambiguous if the removal is lost).

In the rename open, remove manifest.alt with `let _ =` (error ignored) instead of `?`, and also inject a failure into the removal. This checks whether any test holds that a failed removal is answered.

nonblocking: What the diff adds when nothing fails, by function. (1) Maint::land_front (src/db.rs ~40047): the old `out?` became `if let Err(e) = out { if !manifest_slots { stop_seals } ...; return Err }`. That is the same single branch; the stop sits on the cold Err arm. land_durable's only Err is the publish itself, so a later maybe_compact error cannot reach the stop. (2) vault::sync_dir / sync_dir_as (src/db/vault.rs ~2157): the one Relaxed load and branch that sync_dir made after its fsync now happens before it, and the seam work is in a #[cold] #[inline(never)] fn. Same count on every directory fsync: seal landing, rotation, publish. (3) open_slot, sync_slot, sync_file: a bool load became a u8 load and a bit test; these run only on the open path. (4) manifest_write passes a constant to sync_dir_as. Maint::publish is byte-for-byte the base. (5) Db::open under the rename shape with a manifest read: one vault::sync_dir before any removal. This is the brief's allowance (c). (6) Db::sync_pending where pending names were taken, in the clear. This is allowance (d). (7) manifest_make_slots moved ahead of the cipher sweep under the slots: same exists() calls, and an fsync only where a slot file is missing. Nothing on a commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish or read path gains a syscall, wait, lock or allocation.

Beyond the brief's literal allowance, crossing-only. Db::open, rename shape, where manifest.alt is found (src/db.rs ~29046): an unlink of manifest.alt, plus a full rename-shape manifest write (temp write, fsync, rename over `manifest`, directory fsync) where alt was the slot taken. It runs once, on the first rename-shape open after a slots life, never in steady state. It is what closed round 1's blocker (followup 36), and R1/R2/R3 show each part is needed, so I do not hold it blocking. A cheaper shape for the alt-taken case: rename manifest.alt over `manifest`, then one directory fsync. That needs no temp write and fsync, if the v2 slot image reads as the rename shape's `manifest`. Not checked.

Merge, tier and promotion publishes under the rename shape still do not stop the queue when their directory fsync fails, and the account lists this as not built. I checked the argument against the code. compact_run (src/db.rs 13731), the tier merge (13899) and the promotion (41220) each fsync the directory themselves before publish(). Their outputs' entries are therefore durable before the publish, and only the manifest's rename depends on the publish's fsync. blocking.where: src/db.rs:12583-12599 (manifest_make_slots) and its call at src/db.rs ~29075 (Db::open, `if opts.manifest_slots { manifest_make_slots(dir, opts.fail_open_dir_sync)? }`); tests/durable.rs:11334 (a_crossing_slots_open_whose_dir_sync_fails reopens with `Db::open(&x, slots.clone()).is_ok()` and checks nothing more)
blocking.detail: The crossing back from the rename shape is held only by `manifest_make_slots` finding a slot file missing: it `vault::create`s `manifest.alt` and only then fsyncs the directory. That fsync is what makes the rename life's last rename durable. Take a slots open that is killed between the create and the fsync, or whose fsync fails. The `fail_open_dir_sync` seam builds exactly that second case, "with that file made". It leaves `manifest.alt` in the directory. The next slots open then finds both files, makes nothing and fsyncs no directory. The fdatasyncs of the two slot files cover file data, not the rename's directory entry, under the same model the (c) and srs tests use. That open then removes what the unsynced renamed manifest stopped naming, and its publishes write slots in place with no directory fsync. A power cut before the first seal's readable-landing directory fsync can therefore keep the removals and lose the rename. That is the refusal the srs tests failed on in before-r1.log ('the manifest slot manifest names par-..., which is missing'), over acknowledged writes. The existing test reaches the state and stops short: after the failed open it reopens under the slots and asserts only that the open succeeds. It never commits or cuts the power after that reopen. Test to add: a rename life killed between a rename and its directory fsync; a slots open with `fail_open_dir_sync` (or a kill after the create); a slots open without the seam; commits acknowledged; the power cut the (c) tests model. It should fail on the tree as it stands. Smallest fix, on the crossing's cold path only (a slot file missing): fsync the directory before the missing file is created as well as after. The alternative is to make the file under a temp name and rename it into place after the fsync. Either way the file is never visible until the rename life's entries are durable. A slots open with both files present pays nothing more. Until then neither the docs' claim that the slots open "makes it and fsyncs the directory before it removes anything" nor followup 36's closure holds for this state.

nonblocking: A merge's, a tier's or a promotion's rename-shape publish whose directory fsync fails does not stop the queue (land_front alone was changed; join_tier/the merge landing at src/db.rs ~40759 and the promotion at ~41239 return the error after publish_segs). I traced the code and found no state that loses data: the jobs' own directory fsync covers their outputs, the inputs are not retired after a failed publish, and no seal's segments can be between phases at such a publish. Still, the later successful publish's fsync is a retry of a failed directory fsync. Either a test or a sentence in the docs should say why that is acceptable here, since CLAUDE.md says a failed sync is never retried.

The directory-fsync hooks (vault.rs DIR_HOOKS) are keyed by path and pruned only when the store's Shared has dropped. A test that emulates a kill by leaking a Db, then reopens at the same path, would route the reopened store's publish fsyncs through the leaked store's hook and watch closure. The tests appear to copy each state to a fresh directory, so this probably never fires, but I did not check every kill helper.
Mutant r2-D's binary aborted with 'failed to allocate an alternative stack: Cannot allocate memory'. Nobody checked whether a failure path leaks mappings or threads; the implementer says the same.

Consider a directory fsync that fails while a seal's thread has already renamed its segment into place but not yet landed. The seal's later publish then fsyncs the directory again. That fsync can return success over entries the failed one lost, and the publish names the segment and retires the log. CLAUDE.md calls that shape 'a retry is never the remedy'. result.summary:
Built and tested the fix for all three holes in plain stores under EveryN, then priced it, and it does not land under rule 13f.

The three holes: (a) a later commit to the log survives a kill when the closed run's held tail does not; (b) Db::sync answers Ok after a run closes, without covering the run's commits; (c) the same Ok forever once that seal fails.

The fix: close_run takes a cold path (`if self.unsynced != 0` → close_owed). There the writer's thread writes what the run's writer holds, using the new SegmentWriter::write_held, which is sync_with's write half. It then opens the run's temp file afresh, not cloned, so an fdatasync sees a writeback error whatever the seal's own description saw. A ClosedRun goes into Db::closed_runs, with a durable flag the seal job sets after its fsyncs. These syncs cover the closed run first, each in a cold path behind one load and branch:
- Db::sync
- the EveryN due arm of commit, commit_staged, commit_direct and Db::seal
- the seal_rotates_wal branch
- run_again

A failed fdatasync of the closed file wedges the queue and is kept. A close that could not write answers "durable only once its seal lands" until the seal lands.

Tests: eight new tests in tests/durable.rs. Seven fail on the old shape (before.log, before2.log) and all eight pass on the fix (after.log). Neighbours were green: durable 232, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5, segwriter 19, lib 404.

Pricing:
- Rates and reads were level or unresolved everywhere.
- The closing Db::sync phase of supdb-ingestshape at 300k was longer in both sittings: +0.95 and +1.12 ms over 3.4-3.8 ms, with the sittings 0.2-0.4 ms apart. That is a resolved cost under 13e; it is the closed run's fdatasync while its threshold seal is still in flight.
- Alternative 1 (wait for the seal's durable landing) costs more: closing sync 32-33 ms, ordered load 0.72-0.74x in both sittings.
- Alternative 2 only moves the close's write, which was not the cost (the commits phase was level), and it keeps the fdatasync, so it was not built.

Following 13f: the measuring tree's diff (fix, tests, docs, price_* fields, bench arms) is saved as not-landed.patch (also copied to measuring.patch), and the tree is reverted and clean.

Separately, item 7 (stage 0's sync-run fix, landed already): at 10k it costs the ordered load of the arms that close with Db::sync about a third (new at 0.64-0.68x of old in both sittings); at 300k it is level or unresolved.

result.summary: Under EveryN in the clear, a run's due commit synced only the run's file. Log frames that a sync by policy promises stayed unsynced: frames of a hashed table frozen before the run, a log file a rotation left loose, or frames an open replayed (which also covers Always after a reopen). A power cut could then keep the run's commits and lose older commits in the log, which is not a prefix. The fix adds Direct.log_owed, noted once per run in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold). It is set only in the clear (not RUN_LOGGED), as frames_unsynced || loose_wals non-empty. The directory clause is left out, as Db::sync leaves it out. The due branch now asks `if d.log_owed { return self.run_due_log_first(); }`, a load and a branch. The cold path asks the log again and syncs it with sync_wal if it still owes. It then clears the note, syncs the run's file and zeroes unsynced. On that one commit the reference conversion for direct_table_refs is left to the run's next commit. Six tests are in tests/durable.rs, section due-log. Four failed before the fix: frames, loose, reopen-under-Always and fail-order. Two are holding tests and do not count as evidence: a clean log is never synced, and under a cipher the log is synced once, behind the run's frames. No cell of the suite reaches the cold path: the trace counted 0 hits in every sitting and in strace probes of load_only and lag_only. The ordered-load syscalls are identical: fdatasync 303 = 303 durable, 7 = 7 buffered. No pairing resolved a cost; every cell is level or unresolved, so the unit lands. 15 mutants: 14 killed, 1 survived (argued). run-close did not land (its not-landed.patch), so there is no second flag to unify. The two would be one state, "unsynced and older than the open run", noted at the run's open and paid at its first due sync. Work is uncommitted in the tree.
result.shape_landed: The brief's shape. Direct.log_owed: bool is set in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold, once a run) as `mem.after & RUN_LOGGED == 0 && (wal.frames_unsynced() || !loose_wals.is_empty())`. Inside `if due`, `if d.log_owed { return self.run_due_log_first(); }` adds one load and one branch. Db::run_due_log_first is #[cold] #[inline(never)]. It asks the log again (a sync may have paid it since the open) and calls sync_wal() if the log still owes. It then clears the note, syncs the run's file (d.w.sync(), with run_failed on error) and sets unsynced = 0. A failed log sync is answered, kept as Db::lost, and nothing of the run is synced. Under a cipher the note stays false, because log_run's due sync_wal already covers the log behind the run's frames. The hot path's refs block keeps its text from before the unit.

blocking.title: The docs now promise a prefix that an open run still breaks: the helper thread's fdatasync, and plain writeback, make a run's commits durable before the log's older frames
blocking.detail: The diff deletes the named exception ("a crash may lose earlier commits in the log while the run's later ones survive") and puts a general claim in its place: "so a crash that keeps the run's synced commits keeps every commit before them". The SyncPolicy headline now names only the run-close exception. That claim holds only for syncs the policy issues. A direct run's file is a marking segment with a WriterHelper. The helper is spawned once the file reaches SegmentOptions::sync_ahead (8 MiB by default; set_marks keeps the helper and only stops it hashing, src/db.rs:7782-7790 and 6322-6365), and from then on it fdatasyncs the run's file behind the writer whatever the policy is. Take EveryN(n) with n large, including the buffered arm's EveryN(u32::MAX). A hashed table is frozen with its frames unsynced, then a run writes past 8 MiB in commits that are not due. The helper makes those commits durable, markers included. log_owed is asked only at the first due commit, which may never come. A power cut then keeps the run's commits, which the recovery walk accepts up to the last marker that checks, and loses the log's older frames. That is the defect this unit closes, reached by another sync. Kernel writeback of the run file's pages, with no fsync at all, gives the same cross-file non-prefix. The unit's tests do not reach this case: dl_power_cut cuts the run's file to run_synced_bytes, which is the writer's own syncs only, and its runs are a few hundred bytes. The repair is one of two. (a) Keep the exception named, narrowed to what is still true: before the run's first due commit, a power cut may keep run commits that the helper or writeback put on the device and lose older log frames. Keep a ROADMAP item for it, narrowed from the one removed, rather than deleting it. Narrow the CLAUDE.md ordered-ingest paragraph's wording and the Shapes amendment the same way. (b) Close it at a point that is already cold: the helper's spawn happens once per segment. For example, commit_direct could ask d.log_owed where the writer reports that the helper has started, and sync the log there first. That is another syscall on a success path, so it would have to be priced under rule 13. Either way the docs must not claim the prefix for commits synced other than by policy.

blocking.title: The same state is still reachable through the run writer's helper fdatasync and writeback, and the docs now say it is not
blocking.where: src/db.rs:168-173 (SyncPolicy first paragraph), src/db.rs:212-219 (ordered-run paragraph), src/db.rs:6758-6780 and 6323-6350 (WriterHelper, AlignedWriter::landed), src/db.rs:8770-8771 (SegmentOptions defaults early_writeback: true, sync_ahead: 8 << 20); CLAUDE.md ordered-ingest paragraph (~2300); ROADMAP.md item removed
blocking.detail: The fix orders the log ahead of the run's file only at the run's due fdatasync. A direct run's PieceWriter is a SegmentWriter built from Db::segment_opts(&opts), so it carries the default sync_ahead of 8 MiB. Once 8 MiB is written past what is synced, its WriterHelper fdatasyncs the run's file, under any policy and never gated on Direct::log_owed. Every piece is also pushed to the device by sync_file_range (early_writeback), and the commit writes its records before the due branch runs. So under EveryN(n) with a run that passes 8 MiB before its due commit, or under EveryN(u32::MAX), where no commit is ever due (the buffered arm), the helper makes the run's commits durable while the frames of a table frozen before the run (or replayed, or in a loose file) stay unsynced. Recovery walks the temp file to its last good marker, so a power cut then keeps the run's later commits and loses the older log commits. That is exactly the non-prefix state this unit was asked to close. The old SyncPolicy text named the open run as an exception to "an unsynced tail is lost whole and never served in part". The diff deletes that exception and leaves only "a run closed into a seal still in flight". It then says "a crash that keeps the run's synced commits keeps every commit before them", and commits the helper synced are synced commits. Both statements are false as the tree stands, and the removed ROADMAP item was the only place the window was tracked. No test reaches it: every run in the new section is a few hundred bytes, far under sync_ahead. Repair, in order of cost: (a) state the residue truthfully: the open run's commits that reach the device outside the policy's sync (the helper's fdatasync, writeback) may survive a power cut that loses older unsynced log frames. Keep it as an exception in SyncPolicy and the ordered-run paragraph, with a ROADMAP item; or (b) also hold the helper off while d.log_owed is set (cold, at helper spawn, nothing on the hot path), noting that plain writeback still leaves the unacknowledged case; or (c) sync the log where owed before the run's first byte is written, which is a syscall the brief did not price. Whichever is chosen, add a test that holds the state rather than betting on it. Use EveryN(1000) or EveryN(u32::MAX), a small segment.sync_ahead (e.g. 64 KiB), and frozen-table frames unsynced under hold_seal_durable. Commit run batches until the writer's helper flush count moves, wait on that counter and not on a clock, then cut the power to the traced syncs. Read the log's keys against the run's keys for a prefix.

result.summary: Followup 5, repair round 1. The fix from round 0 stands. In the clear, a run's first commit that the policy makes due now syncs the log before the run's file wherever the log owed a sync when the run opened: frames of a table frozen before the run, a file a rotation left loose, or frames an open replayed. This is Direct::log_owed, noted once in commit_direct's run-open branch and checked in the due branch, with a #[cold] Db::run_due_log_first. Both reviewers were right: before that first due sync the run's file also reaches the device by its writer's helper fdatasync (every SegmentOptions::sync_ahead, under any policy) and by kernel writeback. Neither is ordered behind the log, and the round-0 docs claimed a prefix that does not hold there. I chose repair (a): the docs now state the residue truthfully, and nothing on a success path changed. The SyncPolicy headline names the exception again, and the ordered-run paragraph says a crash keeps every commit before one the policy synced, and names the helper and writeback window. The Direct::log_owed doc, CLAUDE.md's ordered-ingest paragraph and the Shapes amendment (which ends in a rule) say the same. ROADMAP.md has a narrowed item back with its two priced shapes. Option (b), holding the helper off, would only narrow the window: writeback remains, and it moves the helper's flushes onto the close. Option (c), syncing the log at the run's open, is a syscall the brief did not price. A new test holds the window with sync_ahead at 64 KiB and waits on the helper's fdatasync count, not a clock (accessor Db::run_device_synced). A power cut there keeps run keys and loses all 150 earlier log keys, and the test asserts that, so whatever closes the window has to restate it. In its second half the first due commit syncs the log first and a cut keeps everything. A second new test came from extra mutant 6, which survived at first and was not equivalent. sync_wal returns errors it does not keep: a loose file's open failing with something other than NotFound, and the header's chain write. Commits go on after such an error, so the note must stay set until the log is synced. The test (the loose file's name made a link to itself during the due commit) kills that mutant. The pricing from round 0 stands and was not run again: this round changed only a test accessor, tests and docs, and neither reviewer showed a pairing failing to reach the mechanism. No cell of the suite reaches the cold path: zero trace lines in every sitting and probe, and strace -c shows identical syscall counts on the ordered load. Neighbours all green: durable 234/234, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5, lib 404; fmt check and clippy -D warnings clean.
result.shape_landed: Direct::log_owed: a bool noted in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold, once a run) as `after & RUN_LOGGED == 0 && (wal.frames_unsynced() || !loose_wals.is_empty())`. The directory clause is left out, as Db::sync leaves it (an owed directory barrier implies a loose file listed). In the due branch: `if d.log_owed { return self.run_due_log_first(); }`, a load and a branch. The cold fn asks the log again, calls sync_wal() if it still owes, clears the note only after the log sync succeeds, syncs the run and zeroes unsynced. Under a cipher the note stays false; log_run's due sync covers it, and a test holds that. Residue named rather than closed (repair a): run bytes the helper's fdatasync or kernel writeback put on the device before the first due sync are not ordered behind the log. The docs and ROADMAP.md say so, and a test holds the helper half. run-close did not land, so there is no second flag to unify. The two would be one state, what is older than the open run and unsynced, noted at the open and paid at the first due sync.

blocking.title: run_again syncs the run's file ahead of a log that log_owed still says is owed
blocking.where: src/db.rs run_again (about lines 30680-30712), reached through commit_direct's nothing-new branch -> run_attended
blocking.detail: Run writes always defer: set_marks sets out.defers, and AlignedWriter::defer returns Ok with the bytes owed. Take EveryN(n>1) with a hashed table frozen before the run and its frames unsynced, so log_owed is true. If the run's non-due commit hits a refused write, it answers Ok and owes the batch. The next call with nothing new for the run (a commit() of nothing, or the commit_staged inside sync/flush) goes run_attended -> run_again. That function does d.w.sync() 'whatever the policy, since the commit that failed may have owed the sync', which stands in for the policy's sync of that batch, then zeroes unsynced. It never consults log_owed or syncs the log first. A commit of nothing then answers Ok with the run's file on the device and the log's older frames unsynced. A power cut after that keeps the run's commits and loses the frozen table's, which is not a prefix, and no exception in the docs names it. Inside Db::sync the same ordering puts the run's sync before the log's. The fix costs nothing on a success path: run_again is already #[cold]. Before d.w.sync(), when the open Direct has log_owed and the log still owes (frames_unsynced or loose_wals non-empty), call sync_wal() and clear the note, the same steps as run_due_log_first. Test, failing first: Frames setup, hold_seal_durable, seal, fail_next_run_write before the run's first (non-due) commit, then a commit of nothing answering Ok, then dl_power_cut. Assert log_missing == 0 whenever any run key is here.

blocking.title: The docs' list of ways a run's bytes reach the device ahead of the log is incomplete: the closing run's presync and its seal job's fsync are missing
blocking.where: src/db.rs SyncPolicy doc lines 171-176 and the ordered-run paragraph 218-228; Direct::log_owed doc (about 5107-5119); close_run presync (30807, 30904-30920, 30933-30949) and the job's seg.sync_all (30866-30876); CLAUDE.md ordered-ingest paragraph (2307-2311); ROADMAP.md item 'A run's commits on the device before its first due sync'
blocking.detail: The SyncPolicy headline says the second exception applies to 'an open run's commits that reach the device before any sync by policy covers them -- by the sync a thread makes behind the run's writer, or by the kernel's writeback', and the other places name only those two ways. Here is a third, found by reading the code. A run in the clear that closes before any due commit, with the log owing (a table frozen before it whose seal is not yet durable), gets its temp file fdatasynced in two places. One is the presync, on the writer's thread at a flush. The other is the run's seal job, on its own thread (vault::persist then seg.sync_all after seal_readable). Neither waits for the earlier seal's durable landing, which the queue orders only at the landings. The temp name stays until a manifest names the run's segment, and recovery reads it. A power cut in that window therefore keeps the run's commits and loses the older table's unsynced log frames: the same non-prefix the round-1 docs name for the helper, for a run that is closing, which the headline's 'open run' wording does not cover. The headline's first exception goes the other direction (the run lost, a later log commit kept). The CLAUDE.md amendment's own corollary ('read against every way the bytes reach the device -- each thread that syncs the file') is not met. Either name the close's syncs in every place that lists the ways and in the ROADMAP item, ideally with a holding test (Frames setup, hold_seal_durable, a short run, a flush with hold_presync, or the seal held at its landing, then a power cut built from the presync's extent), or order them behind the log as well. Syncing the log at the run's open, which ROADMAP already lists, would cover all four ways.

blocking.title: A commit of nothing (and sync/flush via commit_staged) after a failed run write syncs the run's file without the owed log: the defect stays open on run_again
blocking.where: src/db.rs:30691-30712 (Db::run_again), reached from commit_direct's early return at 30404-30406 via run_attended (30672); Db::sync at 31540 calls commit_staged before its own sync_wal
blocking.detail: run_again is the path a commit with nothing new for the run takes when the run's file owes a batch (`SegmentWriter::owes`, set when a piece write failed). Its docs and SyncPolicy's say that call writes the batch again and syncs it 'whatever the policy' before it answers Ok. In the clear it calls d.w.sync() and, only under RUN_LOGGED, the log. It never looks at Direct::log_owed. Here is the scenario under EveryN in the clear: (1) a hashed table's frames are unsynced and the table is frozen with its seal held before its fsyncs; (2) a run opens, so log_owed is true; (3) a non-due commit writes a whole piece (a batch larger than write_piece, e.g. write_piece 4096 as the helper test uses), the device refuses it, and the failure is deferred; (4) a commit with nothing new goes to run_attended, then run_again, which fdatasyncs the run's file, sets unsynced=0 and answers Ok with the log still owing. A power cut there keeps the run's batches, which that Ok promised durable, and loses the older log frames. That is the exact non-prefix this unit was asked to close ("any sync covers everything older first"), and it contradicts the new SyncPolicy text that a crash keeping a synced run commit keeps every commit before it, because the exception the docs name covers only the helper and writeback. Db::sync and flush reach the same function through commit_staged ahead of their own log sync, so they also put the run on the device ahead of the log (unacknowledged there, but a crash between the two syscalls has the same shape). The fix is cold and adds nothing to a success path: in run_again's clear branch, before d.w.sync(), do `if d.log_owed { if log owes { sync_wal()? } d.log_owed = false }`, the same as run_due_log_first, or route the clear case through run_due_log_first. Test it in tests/durable.rs: build the Frames shape with EveryN, write_piece small, fail_next_run_write at a non-due commit that writes a piece, then a commit of nothing answers Ok, then dl_power_cut, then assert log_missing == 0. Run that test on the current tree first and record that it fails.

No new syscall, wait, lock or allocation on a path where nothing is owed. Db::run_device_synced is a test accessor and off every path. Nothing beyond the brief's allowance.

result.summary:
Under EveryN in the clear, a run's due commit used to sync the run's file and not the log. A power cut could then keep the run's commits and lose older log frames: those of a table frozen before the run, a loose file, or frames an open replayed (Always after a reopen). The fix adds Direct::log_owed, noted once in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold), and asked in the due branch (one load and one branch). Its cold path, Db::run_due_log_first, asks the log again, syncs it if it still owes, then syncs the run.

Repair round 2:
(1) and (3) are fixed. Db::run_again is #[cold] and is reached only after a write to the run's file failed. It writes the owed batch again and syncs it whatever the policy, on a commit of nothing, a sync or a flush. It now reads log_owed first: it asks the log again, syncs it, clears the note, then syncs the run. If the log sync fails, that failure is the answer and nothing of the run is synced. New tests (commit of nothing on all run arms, sync, and the failing-log variants) fail on the tree without this fix (before-r2.log): "kept 50 of the run's 50 keys and lost 150 of the 150", and "call 0 answered another error: the run's write failed".
(2) is named, not ordered. A run that closes before its first due commit is synced twice: by the flush's presync and by its seal job's fsync, neither ordered behind the earlier seal's durable landing. This way is now named everywhere the ways are listed: the SyncPolicy headline and ordered-run paragraph, Direct::log_owed, the Db::sync comment, the CLAUDE.md ordered-ingest paragraph and Shapes amendment, and the ROADMAP item. A new holding test builds the window (hold_seal_durable, a short run closed by a flush, the copy taken from another thread while every seal is held, the run's file cut to the presync's extent) and asserts it is open: run keys kept, 150 of 150 log keys lost. Ordering the close behind the log would add a log sync on the close path, which was not priced, so it stays an open ROADMAP item. Syncing the log at the run's open, already listed there, would cover all four ways.
No success path changed this round, so the pairings were not run again. run-close did not land, so there is no second flag to unify. The two flags would be one state, noted at the open.
result.shape_landed: A bool on Direct (log_owed), set in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold, once per run) as `after & RUN_LOGGED == 0 && (wal.frames_unsynced() || !loose_wals.is_empty())`. The due branch checks `if d.log_owed { return self.run_due_log_first(); }` (one load and one branch inside the branch that syncs). The cold Db::run_due_log_first asks the log again, sync_wal()s if it still owes, clears the note, then syncs the run and zeroes unsynced. Db::run_again (cold, only after a failed run write) does the same log-first step before its sync of the owed batch. Under a cipher, log_run's due sync already covers the log, and a test holds that.

These are the helper thread's fdatasyncs (sync_ahead), the kernel's writeback, and, for a run that closes before its first due commit, the flush's presync of its records and its seal's fsync of the file. blocking.title: A log sync error that is not kept leaves a run's batch unsynced and not owed, and a commit with nothing new then answers Ok over it under Always
blocking.where: src/db.rs:30594-30597 (Db::run_due_log_first: `self.sync_wal()?` returns before `d.w.sync()`); src/db.rs:30400-30420 (commit_direct's commit-of-nothing branch asks only `attends()` and `wal.pending`); doc comment at src/db.rs:30582-30591
blocking.detail: `sync_wal` does not keep every error it returns. A loose file's open that fails with anything other than NotFound (db.rs:28171, `Err(e) => return Err(e)`) is returned as is, and so is a failure of `self.wal.chain(..)?` (db.rs:28175). The unit's own test a_runs_due_commit_whose_log_sync_could_not_open_a_loose_file_syncs_it_at_the_next builds that error. When it happens in run_due_log_first, the due commit answers Err. By then its batch is marked committed (`mem.commit()`, visible to readers). The batch's tail is still with the writer, never written, and nothing of it is synced. The writer does not owe it (no write failed, so `attends()` is false), and `unsynced` is not reset. Under SyncPolicy::Always (the reopen case), the next `commit()` with nothing appended takes commit_direct's `committed == len` branch, finds no attention and no pending frames, and answers Ok. No sync runs, of the run or of the log. Before the fix, a run's due commit could fail only at `d.w.sync()`: a write failure leaves the batch owed (run_again, which answers no Ok over it unsynced, as the Db::commit doc promises), and an fdatasync failure is kept. So this state is new. Db::sync and the next due commit with new keys recover it, through the unsynced count and the note that stays set. A commit of nothing under Always does not. The doc on run_due_log_first ('A log sync that fails is the answer and is kept (`Db::lost`)') and the contract-change line '(kept as lost)' are also false for these errors. Smallest repair, cold only: when sync_wal fails in run_due_log_first (and likewise in run_again), set the run writer's owed/held attention bit for its unsynced batch, so the next call with nothing new goes through run_attended -> run_again. run_again already syncs the log first while log_owed stands. Alternatively, keep the error. Then fix the doc wording. The test is extra mutant X1 below.

nonblocking: The before.log and before-r2*.log failures are for the reasons the tests name: kept N of the run's keys and lost all of the log's, and the failed-log variant answering Ok or another error. The tree matches keep/ by sha256 and final-r2.diff byte for byte. The measuring field price_due_log_old and the duelogold arms are gone from src, bench/src and tests (grep finds nothing). I ran the built checked durable binary (built after the sources' mtime) with filter a_runs_, 24 tests listed, under my own TMPDIR: 24 passed, exit 0. I removed the directory afterwards.

The four ways a run's bytes reach the device before its first due sync are left open, named in SyncPolicy, Direct::log_owed, CLAUDE.md and ROADMAP.md, and held by tests that assert the window is open. Those ways are: the helper's sync_ahead fdatasync, kernel writeback, and a run closed before its first due commit (the flush's presync and its seal job's fsync). They are the same class of defect as this unit's: a non-prefix state, though only over commits nobody acknowledged. Syncing the log at the run's open, behind the same note, would close all four for one cold syscall at a run's open over a log that owes. That is worth pricing next rather than keeping four named exceptions.

run_due_log_first returns before the refs tail (`set_run_flushed`, `set_ref`, `upkeep_staging`) for direct_table_refs. That costs memory only: the next commit converts the references. Correctness is not affected.

The note leaves out wal_dir_unsynced. By reading, it can be true with loose_wals empty only after a chained rotation's barrier failed, and that failure is kept (pending_err answers first), so leaving it out is sound. The comment at db.rs:30441 says so.
M10 and O2 (the note not cleared) are argued equivalent: the re-ask finds nothing and the same syscalls run in the same order. Accepted.

The strace counts in strace/ match the account: load_only 300000 1 shows fdatasync 303 and pwritev 335 for both durable arms, and 7 fdatasync for both buffered arms; lag_only shows 627 against 628, and 29 against 29. I did not re-read the pair tables cell by cell. The verdicts are taken from notes.md.
extra_mutants: X1 (test for the blocking item): use the unopened-loose test's shape (a loose file's name made a symlink to itself during the due commit), but under SyncPolicy::Always. A reopen-style or loose-shape store with seal_bytes large enough that no seal falls inside works. After the due commit answers the non-NotFound error, put the loose file back and call db.commit() with nothing appended. Assert that it either answers an error, or answers Ok with run_synced_bytes() moved past 0 and the loose file in wal_syncs_traced() before the run's sync. Expected on the current tree: Ok with run_synced_bytes() == Some(0), so the test fails. Then take a power cut via dl_power_cut and assert that every key of the failed batch reads back if the call answered Ok.

X2: in run_due_log_first, replace `self.sync_wal()?` with a version whose non-kept error also sets the writer's attention bit. Then delete that bit-setting line, so the repair is deleted. X1 must fail on that mutant.
X3: in run_again's log-first block, on sync_wal's error, skip whatever the repair adds (if it marks the writer owed again or keeps the error). X1's sync variant should kill it.

blocking.title: New contract sentence claims a prefix that a run closed into a seal in flight still breaks
blocking.where: src/db.rs:219-223 (SyncPolicy, ordered-run paragraph: "so a crash that keeps a run's commit the policy synced keeps every commit before it"); also the headline exception at src/db.rs:171-173 and the closed-run sentence further down the same paragraph ("a crash then may lose them while a later commit to the log survives"), CLAUDE.md's ordered-ingest paragraph, ROADMAP.md:351-372
blocking.detail: I found this by reading the code; no test builds it. Run A in the clear, under EveryN, closes into a seal (Db::seal, a commit at the threshold, or a write below its greatest key followed by a seal of the hashed table). Its commits since the last sync by policy are still unsynced in A's file, and the seal is held before its durable landing. The live table is now empty, so direct_can_open lets the next key above max_key open run B. B's log_owed comes only from the log (wal.frames_unsynced / loose_wals) and says nothing about A's file. B's due commit syncs the log if the log owes, then B's file. A power cut after that commit keeps B's acknowledged-durable commits and loses A's older unsynced ones, which is not a prefix. The sentence this unit added says without qualification that every commit before a policy-synced run commit is kept. The exception it relies on is worded everywhere as "a later commit *to the log* survives", so it does not cover a later *run's* commit. Two fixes are possible. One is to qualify the new sentence ("every commit of the log before it", or "but for a run closed earlier into a seal still in flight"). The other is to widen the closed-run exception in the SyncPolicy headline, the ordered-run paragraph, the EveryN variant doc, CLAUDE.md and the ROADMAP item to "a later commit, to the log or of a later run, survives". The brief asked whether this unit's flag and run-close's are one state ("what the log or an earlier run owes"). This is the direction that stays open because run-close did not land, and the docs should say so. A holding test like the close test (hold_seal_durable, run A closed by Db::seal, run B to its first due commit, power cut, assert window open) would pin it.

nonblocking: Success-path delta, by function (read off `git diff -U0 src/`): commit_direct's due branch gets one load of d.log_owed and one branch, as the brief allows. commit_direct's run-open branch, once per run, gets a load of mem().after, an AND, Wal::frames_unsynced (two loads and a compare) and loose_wals.is_empty (one load). This is the cold note the brief named. Direct grows by a bool. run_due_log_first and run_again's new block are #[cold] #[inline(never)]. run_device_synced is a #[doc(hidden)] accessor with no field and no store on any path. Db::sync, commit_staged and the CLAUDE.md/ROADMAP edits are comments only. Nothing else is added: no syscall, lock or allocation on a success path.

The pairing cannot see the one cost the brief allowed. In measuring.patch the old arm sets log_owed = !price_due_log_old && ..., so both arms carry the due branch's load and branch, and the cold path ran in neither (0 SUPDB_DUELOG_TRACE lines in every .err and probe). The pairings are an A/A of the due-branch hot path. What they actually price is the run-open note, which the old arm short-circuits. No callgrind count of commit_direct against 3df85d22/0c6748bb was taken. The brief allowed this shape, and an instruction count by function (bench/examples/load_only.rs under callgrind, toggle on Db::commit_direct) would make the 'one load and a branch' claim a count rather than a reading.

The priced tree is not the landed tree. measuring.patch moved commit_direct's refs tail into an #[inline(always)] helper (run_refs) and had the wal_dir_unsynced clause in the note and the re-ask. The landed tree keeps the base's inline text and drops the dir clause. The due branch is the same in both. The notes say this, and the commit message should say it too.

Twins checked by reading: supdb-duelogold and supdb-ingestduelogold differ from supdb and supdb-ingest only in Policy.price -> Options::price_due_log_old. name() returns early on price, but no other twin sets it. The measuring field and arms are out of the tree: grep for price_due_log_old in src/ and bench/src finds nothing.

Per-sitting reading checked on one table only: m-300000 durable shows 2 marks in sitting 1 (seal_sort_ms, upkeep_ms counts, no rate) and 0 in sitting 2, which matches 'no rate marked'. I did not re-read every table's arm order or the ingest tables.

The wal_dir_unsynced clause was dropped from the note, and I checked the argument for it against the code. rotate_wal sets it and either pays it at once (chained) or pushes the closed file to loose_wals (loose). loose_wals is emptied only in sync_wal, after wal_dir_barrier. So a directory barrier owed implies a loose file listed.

run_due_log_first returns before the refs tail and before log_run. Under RUN_LOGGED it is never reached (debug assertion, cipher tests). Under direct_table_refs (supdb-refvals) the references for that one commit are taken at the run's next commit, or never if the run closes, and the table keeps its copies. That is benign, but it is behaviour the arm's hot path did not have.
ROADMAP.md:333 says 'a buffered store's run is never due, so only this thread syncs it'. That holds for the suite's EveryN(u32::MAX), not for EveryN(n) in general. Wording.
Db::commit's doc (src/db.rs ~30145-30172) does not say that a run's due commit may now answer a failed log sync, and so be kept as lost. SyncPolicy's paragraph covers it.
CLAUDE.md's Shapes amendment is long and narrative ('The second review found two more'). The file's manner tolerates this. It ends in a rule.

The Reopen and Loose cases should kill it; check that the Loose case does, since the rotation's commits may have zeroed unsynced at a due sync.

Under the Always-after-reopen shape, run_again's log-first block replaced by nothing only when SyncPolicy::Always (gate the block on `matches!(self.opts.sync, SyncPolicy::EveryN(_))`). The run_again tests run only under EveryN(5), and the reopen tests never drive a failed run write.

A later run's due commit after an earlier run closed into a held seal (the blocking item): not a mutant of the diff but a holding test to add. Without it, a future change to log_owed that also notes an earlier run's owed file would have nothing to restate.

result.summary:
Under EveryN in the clear, a run's due commit used to sync only the run's file. Older log frames that no sync covered could then be lost to a power cut while the run's commits survived, which is not a prefix: frames of a hashed table frozen before the run, a log file a rotation left loose, or frames an open replayed (Always after a reopen of a buffered life). The fix: `Direct::log_owed` is noted once, in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold), as `after & RUN_LOGGED == 0 && (wal.frames_unsynced() || !loose_wals.is_empty())`. The due branch tests it with one load and a branch; its cold path, `Db::run_due_log_first`, asks the log again, syncs it if it still owes, then syncs the run. `Db::run_again`, the sync of an owed batch that stands in for a due one, also syncs the log first while the note stands.

Round 3, blocking item 1, fixed. When `sync_wal` fails in run_due_log_first with an error it does not keep (a loose file that would not open, a failed header chain), the batch was committed and visible but owed by nothing. Under Always, a commit with nothing new then answered Ok with nothing synced. Now the failure marks the batch owed by the run's writer (`SegmentWriter::owe_unsynced`, a cold call to `AlignedWriter::owe`), inside the error branch. The next call with nothing new goes run_attended -> run_again, which syncs the log first and then the run. run_again needed no change: its batch is already owed by the write failure that brought it there, and `sync_wal()?` returns before the note is cleared. The doc comments of run_due_log_first and run_again now say which errors are kept.

Round 3, blocking item 2, docs plus a holding test. This sentence was true only of the log: 'a crash that keeps a run's commit the policy synced keeps every commit before it'. It now reads 'every commit of the log before it (not those of a run closed earlier into a seal still in flight)'. The SyncPolicy headline and the closed-run sentence now say a later commit 'to the log or of a later run' survives. `Direct::log_owed` says the note covers the log alone. The log's frames and a closed run's file would be one state ('what is older than the run and unsynced'), but this unit does not note the second because run-close did not land. CLAUDE.md is amended in two places and the ROADMAP item is widened. A holding test builds the window and holds it open on the fixed tree: run A closed by Db::seal under hold_seal_landing, then run B's due commit, then a power cut that keeps B and loses A.

No success-path code changed this round: the one code change sits on an error path inside a #[cold] fn. No reviewer said a pairing misses the mechanism, so the pairings were not run again. The earlier rounds' verdict stands: no cell of the suite reaches the cold path (0 trace lines in every sitting and probe), and every cell is level or unresolved. Neighbours all pass: durable 243, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5, lib 404. fmt and clippy at -D warnings are clean. Nothing is committed.
result.shape_landed: The brief's shape, as asked for. One bool per run (`Direct::log_owed`) is noted in commit_direct's run-open branch (cold) wherever the log owes: unsynced frames or loose files. The directory clause is left out: a directory barrier owed implies a loose file listed, as Db::sync already argues. The due branch asks the bool with one load and a branch. Its cold path, `run_due_log_first`, asks the log again, sync_wal()s if it still owes, clears the note, syncs the run and zeroes unsynced. On a sync_wal error it marks the batch owed by the run's writer (round 3). `run_again` syncs the log first while the note stands. Under a cipher the note is never taken, because log_run's due sync already covers the log; holding tests and a debug assertion say so. run-close did not land, so there is no second flag to merge. The two would be one state ('what is older than the run and unsynced'), and the docs say the closed-run direction stays open.

result.success_path_cost: On the success path a run's due commit pays one load and one branch (`if d.log_owed`). A run's open pays the cold note: two loads and a compare in a branch that runs once a run. When the log owes, the cost is one log fdatasync at the run's first due commit, plus one at a call with nothing new that writes an owed batch again. The round-3 repair costs nothing when nothing fails: it sits inside sync_wal's error branch in a #[cold] fn. No cell of the suite reaches the cold path, so its cost there is a count of zero, not a rate.

contract_changes: A run's commit in the clear that the policy syncs (every commit under Always, the due one under EveryN) syncs the log first wherever the log owed a sync when the run opened: frames of tables frozen before the run or replayed by an open, or a loose file. A crash that keeps such a commit therefore keeps every commit of the log before it. A run closed earlier into a seal still in flight is not covered: a later commit, to the log or of a later run, may survive while that run's commits are lost.
A call with nothing new that writes an owed run batch again (a commit of nothing, a sync, a flush) also syncs the log first where the run's note stands.

A log sync that fails at such a commit is the answer, and nothing of the run is synced. An fdatasync failure is kept (Db::lost). An error sync_wal does not keep (a loose file that will not open, a failed header chain) leaves the batch owed by the run's file, so the next call with nothing new writes and syncs it, log first, and never answers Ok with nothing synced.

Still open and named in the docs: before the run's first due commit, its helper thread's fdatasync, the kernel's writeback, and a closing run's presync and seal fsync can put run commits on the device unordered with older log frames.
