result.summary:
The defect: a plain direct run's temp file (direct-*.tmp) is created and its commits acknowledged by fdatasyncs of that file only. No directory fsync covers the file's name before the first acknowledgement, under Always, under EveryN at the due commit, at Db::sync, or at the sync that rewrites an owed batch. The open finds a run by that name alone.

What I built: the lazy shape as the candidate.
- Direct.log_owed:bool became owed:u8, with the bits RUN_OWES_LOG and RUN_OWES_DIR. DIR is set when a run opens in the clear.
- The barrier is paid after the run file's fdatasync, in run_due_first (behind the due branch's existing one-byte check), in run_again and in sync_run. run_dir_barrier calls vault::sync_dir_as(dir, DirSync::Run) and keeps a failure via keep_lost.
- The eager shape sits behind price_run_dir_eager, and no barrier at all behind price_run_dir_old.
- Seams: Db::watch_dir_syncs, dir_syncs_watched and fail_next_run_dir_sync. They ride the IO_SEAMS word through a directory hook.

Tests: seven, in the run-dir section of tests/durable.rs. Five failed before the fix at their barrier or answer assertion; two are holding tests (cipher, flush). After the fix all seven pass, the neighbour binaries pass, and the whole suite passes with --no-fail-fast.

- Rates: no ordered-load rate cost resolved for either shape at 10000 or 300000, on either arm pair.
- Mechanism, first commit phase (SUPDB_LOAD_PHASES):

- strace: one directory fsync a run, 0.13-0.36 ms on the writer thread for the lazy shape (issued after the file's fdatasync) and 0.26-0.52 ms for the eager shape. Per key that is about 13-20 ns at 10k keys (one run) and about 1-2 ns for a run of about 150k keys.

nonblocking: Success path, by function, as read from git diff. AlignedWriter::maybe_start_helper / helper_description (src/db.rs:6366-6430): the dup is replaced by reopen(), one openat("/proc/self/fd/N", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC) per helper spawn. That is the brief's one allowed cost. Beside it, once per helper, are one load and branch (helper_fault.is_some_and(refuses)) and two is_some checks that build Option<HelperSeams>. WriterHelper::run (src/db.rs:6955-7020): the per-sync `if let Some(c) = fail` count now sits inside the Err branch, so the success path loses a branch. The new `|| seams.is_some_and(sync_at_stop)` is evaluated only once stop is set, folded into the existing check. SegmentWriter::sync_attended (src/db.rs:7736-7758): the RUN_FAULT_WB test is on the #[cold] path the existing `fault != 0` compare sends it to. Nothing per commit, per sync, per hint or per read.

Seam costs on a seal's or merge's success path that are not folded into an existing check, all once per segment writer and next to a file create. SegmentWriter::create has `if let Some(f) = &opts.helper_fault` (src/db.rs:7435). SegmentOptions and AlignedWriter each gain an Option<Arc<HelperFault>>, cloned by Db::segment_opts and stored at AlignedWriter::new. Db's run open now does a read-modify-write of the fault byte instead of a store (src/db.rs:30727). This matches how fail_helper_syncs was already carried, and CLAUDE.md's precedent of a load and a branch beside a syscall. It is not literally 'folded'. Folding helper_fault into the existing fail_helper_syncs field (one Option for both seams) would take the extra branch and clone off.

Pricing does not show the mechanism ran in the lag sweep. strace and the folio reading were taken over load_only only. At 10k no helper exists (below sync_ahead), and the implementer says so. Whether any seal or merge during the 300k lag sweep's bursts spawned a helper is not shown by a count. Given the change is one syscall swap per helper, the loads (where strace shows openat in the new arm and F_DUPFD in the old) are the cells that price it. Read the lag cells as not reaching the change rather than as level for it.

Measuring twins checked by reading bench-arms.patch: supdb-helperraceold and supdb-ingesthelperraceold differ from supdb and supdb-ingest (Policy {partition:false, durable:false}) only in `price`, which maps to Options::price_helper_race_old. In the measuring patch that field changes only helper_description (try_clone). Every pair.sh run used a bench binary built from that measuring tree (head.txt shows 6f2e8dd3 plus the patch); per notes.md the measuring field and its arms were then removed. The one marked cost cell (upkeep_ms, 300k durable, m sitting 1: new 370 vs old 336, p .039) was rerun. In r2 it read new +2.6% in both sittings, unmarked. In m sitting 2 it read the other way. Unresolved under rule e, and the upkeep thread does not touch the changed code.

Caller-visible change not in the public docs: where /proc/self/fd cannot be opened (no /proc, or a file mode the owner cannot read), SegmentOptions::sync_ahead now starts no helper at all. The writer then syncs and hashes alone. This is tested (a_writer_whose_helper_cannot_open_its_file_writes_without_one), but the doc of `sync_ahead` (src/db.rs:8839-8862) does not say it. ROADMAP.md says it; the crate docs should too.

The new CLAUDE.md corollary (CLAUDE.md:3896-3899, 'where two threads sync one file and either can answer a caller, each syncs through its own open file description') reads against an existing site: the close_presync handle is still a try_clone of the writer's description (Direct writer file_clone, src/db.rs:9131-9133). The presync on the writer's thread and the seal thread's fsync run on that one description. It is safe today only because the landing waits for the writer's answer (SealJob::awaits_writer) and the flush waits for the seal. Either qualify the corollary or say why the presync is exempt.

The tests do not bet on timing. The helper is held in its window by HelperFault::hold_store, with a ReleaseHelper guard declared after db/w, so it drops first and releases on failure. The merge test waits for the merge's start (in ss_store_with_a_merge_due) and then its end. sync_at_stop makes the seal's and the merge's helper take its due sync whatever the thread's timing. The seal and merge tests did not fail before the fix (join_helper was already right). The implementer correctly does not count them as failing-first evidence; they are held by M2 and M3.

nonblocking: I found nothing blocking. src/db.rs:6366-6430 and reopen() at about src/db.rs:9005 replace the helper's try_clone with an O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC open of /proc/self/fd/N. It is made once, where the helper is spawned, and the writer's success path gains nothing else. The writer's own hints are SYNC_FILE_RANGE_WRITE only (start_writeback, src/db.rs:6808), so they consume no errseq on the writer's description. The finish's join_helper still runs before the rename. The kernel behaviour the fix relies on is shown by probe2.out (ext4 over a loop device on a full tmpfs). After the helper's dup fails, the writer's fdatasync answers 0. After the helper's own description fails, the writer's answers ENOSPC. That probe is the only real-device evidence, as the implementer says.

I checked the measuring field: grep finds no price_helper_race_old and no helperraceold in src/, bench/src or tests/, and bench/ has no changes. In measuring.patch, both twin arms set only the price flag.

I ran the six new tests by exact name under my own TMPDIR, from the checked durable binary built after the last source edit (06:24 against 06:23). 6 passed, exit status 0. before.log Part B shows both store-level run tests failing at tests/durable.rs:13736 with the old shape forced, and Part A shows the writer-level test failing at 13793. The seal and merge tests passed before the fix and are honestly not counted as failing-first evidence. In mut-M2 and mut-M3 they fail at 13870 and in ss_commit_answer.

Mutant M7 (/proc path digits reversed) is killed only because the cipher test's run file happens to get a two-digit descriptor. In production a wrong fd would point the helper at another file, so it would hash and sync the wrong bytes. A test that forces the writer's fd to two and three digits, for example by opening dummy fds first, would hold it on purpose.

The seam models the kernel only in SegmentWriter::sync_attended (src/db.rs:7748). The close presync (file_clone, a dup of the writer's description) and the finish's fsync are not modelled. The finish is covered by join_helper. A presync that returns Ok while the helper is in its window is covered by the seal's failure and the stopped queue, by reading only: no test drives that interleaving.

If reopen fails for any reason (EMFILE or EACCES as well as no /proc), the writer silently runs with no helper (src/db.rs:6373). That is correct but slower, and nothing counts it. A counter would make a lost helper visible in the suite.

HelperSeams::sync_at_stop makes an armed helper take a sync after a stop has been asked. It runs only under the seam, and it is what makes the seal test deterministic. It is still a behaviour the production helper never has, and the docs on HelperFault::arm say so.

result.summary:
Repair round 1 is finished, picking up after the 07:10 restart. Nothing is committed and nothing is pushed.

The fix (shape 1): the helper thread behind a segment writer now syncs through an open file description of its own. AlignedWriter::helper_description calls reopen(), which opens /proc/self/fd/N with O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC, building the path on the stack, once where the helper is spawned. If that open fails, the writer runs with no helper and syncs and hashes alone. Because the descriptions differ, a writeback error the helper's fdatasync meets is also reported to the writer's own fdatasync, so a run commit that returns before the helper has stored its error answers the failure itself.

The seam is HelperFault (SegmentOptions::helper_fault: #[doc(hidden)] pub, no cfg, free when unset). It fails the helper's sync by description and checks with kcmp whether the writer's sync is on another description. It can hold the helper between its syscall and its store, can start the helper only after the stop, and can refuse the reopen. Db's run open now ORs its fault byte into the writer's instead of assigning it.

Tests are in tests/durable.rs, in the helper-race section, and in the lib's streaming_writes module:
- The trace "1 B B Y": a run commit beside a helper sync that met the error, plain and under a cipher.
- A writer-level marked sync.
- A writer whose helper cannot open its file.
- A seal's output whose helper sync failed: no manifest names it, flush and settle answer the error, reopen replays.
- A merge's piece whose helper sync failed: nothing lands.
- Round 1 added a sync taken at the stop, the helper's own description checked at writer fds of 2, 3 and 4 digits (readable and close-on-exec), and a lib test that a writer with no helper keeps its own checksum row.

What this round did:
- **Extra mutants:** all eight distinct ones (E1–E9) were run. E5 and E7 survived at first; each now has a test and is killed. E6 survived because its check (`told_other`) could not be reached, so the check was taken out.
- **Pricing again:** the helper's spawn had been restructured on the writer's path, so the pairings were rerun (pairs-r1). The second stamped pairing (st2) split, so no cost is resolved.
- **Measuring field and arms:** taken out; the tree's sums match keep/sha256.txt.
- **CLAUDE.md:** the round's paragraph is finished.
- **Format and clippy:** fmt applied, and one clippy fix in a test (is_none_or).
- **Tests:**
  - The whole suite ran with --no-fail-fast and exited 0 (20 binaries).
  - After the fmt and clippy edits, clippy, durable, segwriter and lib were run again and all exited 0.
  - The unit's TMPDIR has been removed.

Shape (2), the in-flight count, was not built, because shape (1) resolved no cost.

nonblocking: Pricing, rule 13e (no change asked): in st1 the durable 300k ordered stamped pairing had fsync-after-readable longer for the new shape in both sittings (+270 and +207 us), and the sittings differed from each other by less than that. Read literally, that is a resolved cost, provided the phase holds the change. The implementer argues it does not: the durable arm's helper makes no sync, and the only change on that path is one openat at the helper's spawn, long before the fsync. The folio walk found identical page-cache composition. st2 then split (new shorter in s1, longer in s2). I accept this reading. The commit message should still report st1's both-sitting result next to st2, not just 'unresolved'.

tests/durable.rs, a_helpers_description_is_its_own_at_every_width_of_the_writers_descriptor: the test holds about 1000 /dev/null descriptors so that the writer's file gets a 4-digit fd. The test binary runs tests in parallel. Here the soft RLIMIT_NOFILE is 20000, so it is harmless. Under the common default soft limit of 1024 it would starve the other tests of descriptors (EMFILE). It would also make other writers' helper reopen fail, and that failure falls back to no helper silently. The test could check `getrlimit` and skip the 4-digit width, or raise the soft limit first.

src/db.rs AlignedWriter::landed / helper_description: when /proc is not mounted (some chroots or minimal containers), every segment writer now runs with no helper, silently. The writer's closing fsync then pays the whole flush. Before, the helper ran on a dup. The ROADMAP item names the fallback, but nothing counts it. A counter, or a mention in the Options/SegmentOptions docs, would let an operator see it.

src/db.rs reopen(): on targets other than Linux it falls back to try_clone, which is the old single-description shape. The docs (engine.md, ROADMAP, CLAUDE.md, WriterHelper's doc) say the helper has a description of its own without qualification. The engine is probably Linux-only in practice (memfd, /proc), so this is wording only.

HelperFault::reaches answers the error to every later sync of the writer, where Linux reports it once per description. The doc explains why this is unobservable: the writer keeps RUN_ATTN_LOST and asks the seam nothing after. That holds only as long as sync_attended answers held/lost before it asks the seam; if that order changes, the seam silently becomes stricter than the kernel.

The fix for the real race depends on kernel behaviour that the store's tests do not exercise: on concurrent syncs, the writer's fdatasync waits on the helper's in-flight writeback and then checks its own errseq. probe2 checks this only sequentially, on ext4 on 6.18.44. The concurrent ordering rests on reading the kernel (file_write_and_wait_range waits on PG_writeback before file_check_and_advance_wb_err). This is listed under not_verified and is correct to leave there.

Coverage by policy and path: the store-level '1 B B Y' test runs under EveryN(2) only. Always is covered by stage 0's count-seam tests, not by the description seam. Seal and merge are tested only with background segment work, not inline. The fix is in the shared sync and join path, so these gaps are low-risk, but the brief asked for them to be walked.
extra_mutants: In WriterHelper::run, open the helper's description and then sync on it only for the seamed instantiation, while the unseamed spawn::<false> keeps calling try_clone of the writer's file (e.g. pass `self.file.try_clone()` instead of `desc` in the else branch). The production shape would regress while every seamed test still passes. Expect it to survive: every test uses a seam. If it survives, add a test with no seam that checks via kcmp/fds_on that a helper's fd is another description, e.g. using fail_helper_syncs or a plain writer past sync_ahead.

In SegmentWriter::create, set `out.fault |= RUN_FAULT_WB` only when helper_fault is armed at create, not whenever it is present. The merge test arms later, in before_second, so its writer is created after arming; a run created before arming would miss the bit. Run it to see whether any test creates its writer before arming.

In HelperFault::helper_sync, record `met` after the hold instead of before it, so the window is open while nothing has been met. Expected to be killed by the '1 B B Y' tests. It confirms the tests read `met` inside the window, not after release.

nonblocking: What the diff adds where nothing fails, by function. AlignedWriter's helper spawn (src/db.rs about 6366-6420), once per writer that reaches sync_ahead: helper_description (6443) loads helper_fault and branches, then calls reopen (9048), which is one openat of /proc/self/fd/N with O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC and the path on the stack. That openat is the one thing the brief allows. The thread exit later closes the descriptor; the old dup was closed there too. The spawn also adds one branch on fail_helper/helper_fault to pick spawn::<true> or spawn::<false>. Nothing is added per commit, per sync or per read. sync() still makes its single `fault != 0` compare, and RUN_FAULT_WB (0x10) is set only by the seam, so the cost only falls on the cold path.

Small additions outside the brief's openat, none on a per-operation path. (a) SegmentWriter::create (src/db.rs:7478-7481) adds an `if let Some(helper_fault)`, a load and a branch per writer created. (b) Db's run open (src/db.rs:30771) turns `fault = take(..)` into `fault |= take(..)`, which adds a load of a byte just stored, once per run open. (c) SegmentOptions is one Option<Arc> larger, so each Db::segment_opts clone does one more load and branch. (d) WriterHelper::run (7034) adds `seams.is_some_and(sync_at_stop)`, asked only once stop is true, on the helper thread. None of these is on a commit, sync, flush, read or publish path. Each runs once per writer or run, beside what was already there, so I do not count them as blocking. A stricter reading of rule 1 could question (b).

Pricing, read against rule e. The st1 stamped durable pairing at 300000 read the ordered fsync-after-readable longer for the new shape in both sittings: new 4536/4536 us against old 4266/4329, gaps of +270 and +207 us, larger than the 0 and 63 us between sittings. By the letter of rule e that resolves a cost if that phase holds the change. The implementer argued it does not, and reran (st2), which split. I agree the phase does not hold the change. It is the seal thread's fsync after the readable landing. The helper is joined, and its O_RDONLY description closed at thread exit, before the rename. An O_RDONLY description also avoids ext4_release_file's FMODE_WRITE flush. Round 0, on code before the spawn was restructured, read the same phase shorter for the new shape in both sittings. So the verdict stands, but the commit message should give all three readings rather than present st2 alone as 'split'.

I re-ran phases.py over pairs-r1. The commits phase, where the openat lands on the writer's thread, is split in both stamped durable pairings: 163.6/151.7 then 154.5/159.4, and 159.7/173.5 then 171.5/168.0 ms. The durable shuffled drain, where seal and merge helpers do sync, read 267.0/259.4 then 257.0/253.6 in st1: longer in both sittings, but by 7.6 and 3.4 ms, less than the 10 ms between sittings. st2 read it shorter (258.6/261.7). The buffered shuffled drain is split. So nothing is resolved. The m1 tables have no cell marked in both sittings. Both twin arms in measuring-r1.patch differ from supdb and supdb-ingest only in `price`. name() returns early for the twins, but nothing in bench keys behaviour on more than the 'supdb' prefix. The measuring field and the arms are out of the tree: every file's sum matches keep/sha256.txt, and grep finds no price_helper.

At 10000 keys no helper exists, because files stay under sync_ahead of 8 MiB. Those pairings therefore cannot price the change, and the notes say so. The lag sweep's 1% and 10% bursts at 300k also seal below 8 MiB, so only the full rewrite reaches a helper. The strace counts come from load_only alone, so they show the openat for runs and seals, not for merge pieces.

Behaviour change where /proc is not mounted: every writer now runs with no helper, so no syncs go ahead of the writer and the writer hashes its own row. Before, the dup worked there. This is sound and slower; the ROADMAP item says it. A failed try_clone (EMFILE) used to be the write's error and now silently means no helper.
tests/durable.rs:14002: an assert message carries a run of spaces where a line continuation was lost ('of its own              (writer's fd ...'). Cosmetic.

The HelperFault seam's same_description (src/db.rs, after reopen) and the width test both assert that kcmp succeeds. Under a seccomp profile that blocks kcmp, such as Docker's default without CAP_SYS_PTRACE, every test that uses the seam would panic rather than fail cleanly. That affects tests only; nothing in the engine calls it.

The width test (tests/durable.rs:13943) holds about 1000 descriptors open to reach a 4-digit fd while other tests run in parallel. That is fine at this box's `ulimit -n` of 20000. On a host with the common soft limit of 1024 it would be marginal.

Not checked: the whole-suite claim (I read only r1final's notes), the mutant logs beyond their summaries, the folio walk and the strace logs themselves, kernels other than 6.18 and filesystems other than ext4 for reporting the error to both descriptions, and the non-Linux try_clone fallback.

nonblocking: What runs when nothing fails, by function (src/db.rs). AlignedWriter::landed (~6366): it calls helper_description, which makes one is_some_and branch on helper_fault and then reopen(). reopen (~9040) builds the path on the stack with a loop of divides and makes one openat(O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC), in place of try_clone's F_DUPFD_CLOEXEC. Choosing spawn::<true>/<false> costs a branch, fail_helper.is_some() || helper_fault.is_some(), which replaces the Option clone that was there before. All of this runs once per helper spawn. SegmentWriter::create (~7478) adds one `if let Some(f) = &opts.helper_fault` branch, and AlignedWriter grows one Option<Arc> word, which costs a store at construction and a branch at drop; both are once per segment writer. Db's run open (~30771) turns an assignment into a read-modify-write, once per run. On the helper thread, run() adds `seams.is_some_and(sync_at_stop)` behind `!stop`, so it is only evaluated once a stop is asked, and the counted() call moved inside the Err arm. The writer's sync path adds nothing: the RUN_FAULT_WB test sits inside sync_attended, which is #[cold] and only reached behind the existing `fault != 0` check. Every addition runs once per writer, beside an open syscall, and none runs per commit, sync, hint or read. Strictly, the create-time branch and the extra struct word are not folded into a check the path already made. They are of the kind CLAUDE.md accepts where something is made, so I do not count them as blocking.

With RUN_FAULT_WB set, every write of a seamed writer goes through run_write_fault and pwritev_at, including the at==0 head-split write. The tests' files are therefore written in different pieces (folios) from production's. This is test-only, but a seamed test is not a folio-faithful test.

ROADMAP.md ~228 says 'the store over such a device is the item above', but the item directly above is the zeroed-first-sector item. The dm-flakey item is the one at ~165-179 ('A failed sync held on a device...' / 'its own or the helper's behind the writer'). Name it explicitly.

On non-Linux, reopen falls back to try_clone, which keeps the race. The docs mention the fallback only in reopen's doc comment, and neither ROADMAP nor the crate docs name it as a remaining exception. Linux is the only supported target, so this is a wording gap.

same_description asserts that kcmp works. In a container whose seccomp profile denies kcmp, or on a kernel without CONFIG_CHECKPOINT_RESTORE, every HelperFault test panics with 'kcmp:' instead of failing the assertion it names. This is test-only, since production never reaches reaches().

reopen goes through libc::open directly, not through the vault door. It reopens an already-open descriptor, not a path in the store directory, so the door's purpose is not violated. Still, the door's source-scan test (the_engine_names_no_file_but_through_the_door) evidently does not see libc::open; that is worth a comment at the call site.

nonblocking: CLAUDE.md, the amended entry under 'A sync whose error the next sync could not see' (around lines 3878-3907): the new corollary ('where two threads sync one file and either can answer a caller, each syncs through its own open file description') reads as false against the close's presync, which still syncs through a duplicate of the writer's description (close_run's w.file_clone()) beside the seal thread's fsync on that same description. By my reading that pair is safe, because the flush waits for both answers (awaits_writer and the wedge) before it answers, so the hole the rule names cannot open there. Under O_PATH the access mode reads 0 == O_RDONLY in fdinfo, so the accmode assertions pass, and the helper's fdatasync and preads fail with EBADF in production. If it survives, the noseam test needs to assert that the helper made a successful sync (flushes > 0 with no error).

In ensure_helper, call helper_description() after self.own_on is cleared, keeping the early return (the same shape as E7, but placed after hands_over is computed and own_row_so_far taken). This checks that the no-helper fallback keeps the row on every arm, not only the arm E7 moved.

result.shape_landed: Shape (1): the helper syncs and reads through an open file description of its own. AlignedWriter::landed calls helper_description() -> reopen(&file) once, where the helper is spawned: open("/proc/self/fd/N", O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC), path on the stack, Linux only (elsewhere try_clone). If the open fails, there is no helper: helper_done is set, and the writer keeps its own checksum row and syncs alone. The helper's File is closed when the thread ends. Nothing is added per commit. Seams are behind WriterHelper::spawn::<SEAMED> and a cold sync_attended branch (RUN_FAULT_WB).

contract_changes: The segment writer's helper syncs and reads through its own open file description of the file, opened once at its spawn (/proc/self/fd/<n>, O_RDONLY|O_CLOEXEC). A writeback error its fdatasync meets is therefore also reported to the writer's description, and a run commit or sync is no longer acknowledged over a failed helper sync whose error was not yet stored.
If the helper's open fails, the writer runs with no helper and hashes its own checksum row and syncs alone. It is not an error.
A failed helper sync at a seal's or a merge's finish is the landing's failure, held by tests: no segment under a live name, no manifest names it.

result.summary: Followup 17 is priced. It is the ordering stage 0 landed unpriced: a drain's run job (SealJob::awaits_writer) lands durable only at the writer's Drain ask, after the presync. It was paired against a measuring arm that restores the old landing (land whenever the seal thread has returned). No rate moved in either sitting of eight pairings: ordered and shuffled load, durable and buffered, 10k and 300k. The stamps show why. In 207 of 208 stamped drains the writer's presync returned, and the Drain ask arrived, before the seal thread's trailer fsync. So in both shapes the durable landing runs from join_seal inside the ask. The phase that holds the change (joined minus max(fsynced, presynced)) reads level. strace -f -c shows the same count of every file syscall in both arms. One cell read worse: the durable ordered load at 300k, in the drain's 'readable' stamp, by 0.6-2.6 ms in all four sittings of two stamped pairings. That stamp falls before the first instruction in which the arms differ, and the buffered pair read the same stamp shorter. So it is recorded as unresolved and argued to lie outside the change. Nothing of the order changes, and the 'ok' alternative was not built. Followup 19: the presync's two test seams (fail_presync AtomicBool, swapped unconditionally on the writer path, and a presync_hold load) are now one byte, Shared::presync_seam (PRESYNC_FAIL | PRESYNC_HOLD). Each presync path loads it once and takes a #[cold] Db::seamed_presync when it is set. Followup 21 cannot happen in the current code: seal()'s ordered branch ends in close_direct, which waits for room before it takes the run, and close_run returns nothing, so the Drain ask follows every awaits_writer hand-over. A comment in Db::flush says so. A debug assertion of it was tried and fired in the gate on a correct state: a flush after a presync failure finds the earlier job at the front of the stopped queue. It was taken out. Followup 12: debug_assert!(!awaits_writer || draining) added in Db::hand_seal. CLAUDE.md's presync paragraph is amended with how the ordering was priced and the rule that follows. Four tests added. All four pass before and after, so none is evidence of a fix; the seams test kills the seam mutants. Mutants: 11 run, 10 killed. If that assert fires, the lifter panics with PRESYNC_HOLD still set, and the writer, parked in seamed_presync, never returns from db.flush(). So a red run of this test hangs instead of failing. CLAUDE.md's rule is that 'a test that parks a thread lets it go on its own failure'. One phase read longer in all four sittings: the 'readable' stamp in the durable 300k ordered drain. That phase comes before every instruction the arms differ in, so I recorded it as unresolved and did not build the 'ok' alternative. Followup 19: the presync seams are now one AtomicU8 (PRESYNC_FAIL | PRESYNC_HOLD), loaded once with Acquire. If it is nonzero, the presync goes to a cold Db::seamed_presync (hold wait where `holds`, then fetch_and of the fail bit). The writer's path loses an unconditional atomic read-modify-write. Followup 21 cannot happen in the code as it stands: seal()'s ordered branch ends in close_direct, which waits for room before it takes the run and then cannot fail, so a Drain ask follows every awaits_writer hand-over. A comment in Db::flush says so. The debug assertion I first built for it fired on a reachable state (an earlier job at the front of a stopped queue) and was taken out. Round 1 (no blocking items): I ran every extra mutant. That needed four new tests in tests/durable.rs and two seams moved from Db to Reader (failed_presync_extent, fail_next_presync), so a handle's thread can read and arm them while the writer is held. Db still reaches both through Deref. The seam tests now use ps_watchdog, which lifts a forgotten hold after 30 s and fails the test. If its own lift does not free the flush, it ends the process with a message on stderr. So a missing or broken lift is a failure, not a hang. One reading of mine was wrong and a test corrected it. I first thought a store whose presync had failed never presyncs again, which would make the one-shot fail bit impossible to observe. The new test showed that a stopped queue still takes a later run's close while the frozen list has room, and presyncs it. So the consumption is observable and stays, and an_injected_presync_failure_is_taken_once(+_inline) holds it. Every mutant was killed in the end. X5 (hold after the fail check) survived my first test and is killed by a_failure_armed_under_a_held_presync_is_taken_at_its_lift. X8 hung in round 1a and is killed by the watchdog's exit in round 1b. result.summary:
I priced followup 17 and found no resolved cost. The rule is that a drain's run job (SealJob::awaits_writer) is named durable only when the writer asks, after the writer's own presync (its fdatasync of the run's records). In 207 of 208 stamped drains the writer's ask arrived before the seal thread returned, so the old shape and the new one both land the job from that ask (join_seal). Nothing of the order changed, so the cost reviewer's alternative (an "ok" the writer stores after its presync) was not built.

Item 19 landed: the presync's test seams are now one byte (AtomicU8) loaded once. Before, every presync on the writer's thread did a load plus an unconditional atomic read-modify-write; now it does the one load. Item 21 cannot be reached as the code stands. When seal() takes the ordered branch it ends in close_direct, which waits for room before it takes the run and cannot fail after that, so every hand-over of an awaits_writer job is followed by the flush's Drain ask. A comment in Db::flush says this. A debug assertion of it was tried in round 0, fired on a state that can happen and is correct (an earlier job at the front of a stopped queue), and was taken out. Item 12 landed as a debug assertion in Db::hand_seal.

Round 1 added seam tests and a watchdog so a forgotten hold fails the test instead of hanging it. Round 2:
(a) A held writer presync now sets a PRESYNC_WAITING bit for as long as it waits; this is only inside the cold seamed_presync path. Reader::presync_hold_state reads it, and the three tests that lift the hold now wait for the writer to be at the hold before checking anything. Extra mutant 2 is now killed by that wait ("the writer's presync never waited at the hold"), not by the 100 ms sleep.
(b) The inline test now checks that the hold it armed is still armed after a presync that hold did not hold. This kills extra mutant 4.
(c) Two doc paragraphs belonging to hold_seal_landing and fail_next_landing had been sitting on seamed_presync's doc since before this unit; they are moved to their own functions.

All five extra mutants were run. Mutant 1 is killed as expected. Mutant 3 is killed by 12 tests but survives with a_drain_names_its_runs_segment_durable_before_it_answers run alone, which confirms that test is not evidence. Mutant 5 survives as an equivalent mutant: awaits_writer always implies draining, enforced by the item-12 assertion. My own O1-O5 on the new lines are all killed.

The full suite (--no-fail-fast, 20 binaries) passes, lint passes, and formatting is clean. Nothing this round changed what runs when nothing fails, so the pricing was not rerun.
result.shape_landed: Order unchanged: an awaits_writer job still lands durable only at the writer's Drain ask, after its presync. The presync's test seams are one AtomicU8 (PRESYNC_FAIL=1, PRESYNC_HOLD=2, PRESYNC_WAITING=4), loaded once by each presync path; a nonzero byte takes the cold Db::seamed_presync. That function waits at the hold and sets/clears WAITING only when it was called with `holds` and the hold is armed, then consumes the failure bit with fetch_and. There is a debug_assert!(!awaits_writer || draining) in Db::hand_seal. Item 21 has no code change, only a comment in Db::flush explaining why the ask always follows.

result.summary:
Priced the costs stage 0 added to Db::open and folded the ones that were free to fold; nothing on a success path of a commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish or read changed. The changes:
(1) manifest_read_all now returns the slot files it opened, and the open fdatasyncs those same descriptors. vault::open_slot_found is gone, so each slot file is opened once.
(2) The directory is listed once and sorted. That one listing serves on_disk, the log/spare loop and unnamed_refusals' run temp names, where before the open listed the directory three times. A plain store checks whether a named segment is there with a binary search of the listing. Under a cipher the listing is the vault's names, so vault::on_device's stat stays.
(3) unnamed_refusals now runs right after open_refusals, before the log replay (followup 39).
(4) unnamed_refusals looks an unnamed segment's last key up only in the named segments, and runs' segments, whose name fences take the key in (Db::name_takes, the same [lo,hi) a read routes by). Each candidate is mapped once and cached, and the search stops at the first holder (followup 57).
(5) vault::note adds trace records for the open's own reads (read_slot, on_device, open_holder, replay). They sit on open-only paths, cost one relaxed load when the trace is off, and are what the tests count.

Evidence:
- Five tests failed before the fix (before.log), one cipher test that is held passes before and after, and all six pass after (after-unit.log).
- The whole suite with --no-fail-fast passed on the measuring tree (after.log). durable, db, cipher, fuzz, lib, clippy -D warnings and fmt --check passed on the landing tree.
- 26 mutants: 25 killed, 1 survived (N10, a cost-only mutant).
- Pricing used a probe of the suite's store, opened a few hundred times with three alternating shapes over the same files: folded (this fix), landed (stage 0 as it stands) and bare (no slot syncs and no checks). Folded is about 1.5-2% faster than landed at 10k keys in both sittings and level at 300k and 3M. The suite's pairs read level.
- Stage 0's own price (bare vs landed) is about 120-150 us of a ~500 us open at 10k (the two fdatasyncs, which stay), 2-4% at 300k, and level at 3M. After a crash that leaves a merge's outputs unnamed, the open is 1.5-1.6x the bare shape. Folding the check to the right segments did not move that, and the remainder is not attributed; a ROADMAP item is added for it.
- Syscalls in one open at 10k keys: 166 landed, 151 folded, 149 bare.
- The work is left uncommitted. The measuring field, the four bench arms and the probe are out of the tree and kept in measuring.patch.
result.shape_landed: The open reads each manifest slot file once and fdatasyncs it through the descriptor its read opened. It lists the directory once, sorted, and every name check and sweep reads that listing. In the clear, whether a named segment is there is answered from the listing; under a cipher each envelope is still looked for (vault::on_device). The unnamed-segment check runs before the log replay, and looks an unnamed segment's last key up only in the named segments and runs' segments whose name fences take the key in (Db::name_takes), each mapped once. The order is kept: both slots are made durable before anything is removed or written, and nothing is removed before the slot is checked.

blocking.title: The test named for one open of each slot file does not hold it: N10 survives
blocking.detail: an_open_opens_each_slot_file_once (and its cipher twin) counts `vault::note("read_slot")` records, and the only place that note is made in the landing tree is manifest_read_all's own open. The test failed before the fix only because the measuring tree put the same note into the old `open_slot_found` (measuring.patch, vault.rs hunk). Nothing in the landing tree notes a second open, so a regression that reopens each slot by path for its fdatasync passes. That is the unit's own mutant N10, which survived, and the unit's main fold is then held by reading and by a one-off strace count alone. This is a test that does not test what its name says. Fix it in one of two ways. (a) Make it hold the fold: have `vault::sync_slot` record which descriptor it synced (its raw fd, or the (dev, ino, fd) triple) next to the one manifest_read_all noted at the read, and assert they match. A by-path reopen while the read's File is still alive gets a different fd, so N10 dies. (b) Rename the test to what it does hold (each slot file read once, both made durable) and list N10 as unheld. Rule 6 asks for (a). Re-run N10 against it.
blocking.where: tests/durable.rs an_open_reads_each_slot_once / an_open_opens_each_slot_file_once (+_under_a_cipher), ~14800; src/db/vault.rs sync_slot (~1980) and note (~2257); src/db.rs manifest_read_all 13142

nonblocking: Correctness walk, done by reading: (1) The slot fold syncs the same inode the read took. Nothing renames or writes a slot between manifest_read_all and the sync loop. pending_whole only reads. A torn slot's file is kept (files[i] is set before the parse), so the other slot is still synced 'whatever it read as'. alt_found is equivalent to before. An absent file is still not made. (2) The single listing is taken after both slot syncs, and nothing between it and the old second and third listings writes into the directory, because replay only reads. So on_disk, the wal/spare loop and the runs' temp names see the same set as before. (3) Moving unnamed_refusals ahead of the replay is sound: it reads nothing the replay produces. It still runs before any removal or slot write, and before the rename shape's directory fsync, so a refusal removes nothing. (4) name_takes matches Seg::open's fence parse (4 fields, unhex lo, empty hi unbounded) and Seg::may_hold's [lo,hi). seg- names and names that fail to parse take every key (conservative). A truncated fence is at or below every key that shares its prefix, so no holder's own key is excluded. A key a segment holds outside its name's fences is one no read can reach either, so the routed check can only refuse where the old check accepted a key reads could not serve. No crash state builds that. Kernel mode takes the plain listing path (held is None), which is right because the kernel's names are plaintext. The cipher arm is unchanged where it cannot fold (on_device stays) and folded where it can (slot descriptors).

I did not run any test. The durable test binary under target/checked (12:52) is older than src/db.rs (12:53, put back by the mutant runner), so it may hold the last mutant (X2). The working tree's sums do match keep/sha256.txt. after.log (whole suite, --no-fail-fast) was run on the measuring tree. Only durable, db, cipher, fuzz and lib were re-run on the landing tree, so the other test files (blob, segwriter, zpages, dirkey, ...) were not run on the tree that lands. They are worth running once at the commit.

Tests that copy a live store: an_open_after_a_crash_reads_only_the_segments_over_an_unnamed_segments_keys holds the merge's landing across copy_store. After the flush, though, the segment work still owes the drain's slot fdatasync and the WAL's retirement, and nothing holds them. If they fall inside the copy, the copy is either still a crash state (slot written, log gone or present) or copy_store fails on a file that vanished. It never yields a wrong state, but CLAUDE.md asks for every landing that could fall inside to be held. I did not check whether those steps can still be pending once merge_waits_at_landing is true. an_open_that_refuses_an_unnamed_segment_replays_no_log_first copies after settle plus a one-put commit, with nothing in flight. That is fine.

The probe's 'landed' variant (measuring.patch) is faithful for the unnamed check: without route it maps every candidate at the first key and does not break, as stage 0 did. The 'bare' variant skips both slot syncs and both checks. The 1.5-1.6x open after a crash is stage 0's cost, unattributed, and is filed in ROADMAP rather than folded. It should be in the owner's report as a resolved cost of stage 0 (open-order), not of this unit.

Rule 13d (stamped pairing, strace over load_only) was not built. The argument holds, since no suite phase opens a store and the brief's probe plus strace of one open replace it. The suite pairs on --passes load are a control only, and they read level.

A fourth directory listing is left: the direct-tmp loop at src/db.rs ~29605 calls vault::names(dir) again, after the slot write. Whether it could read `listed` depends on whether anything between makes or removes a direct- temp name. It is not required by the brief. The summary's 'listed once' is of the three checks' listings, which is accurate.

CLAUDE.md's new entry 'A check added to the open, priced by nobody' carries near-figures ('a quarter of an open of a small store'). It also calls the fold 'a step under what a pairing resolves at every size', where the probe read folded 1.5-2% faster at 10k in both sittings. Wording, not a false claim. Two doc comments got over-long unwrapped lines: Db::open's 'is read, and only in the segments ... Under a cipher such a segment's envelope' and unnamed_refusals' 'Made before the log is replayed ... One with writes past what the slot covers'. Rewrap them.

before.log records an_open_under_a_cipher_looks_for_each_named_envelope as FAILED, at durable.rs:9065 ('a plain slot of this version'), a helper assertion unrelated to the fold. before-cipher-named.log has it passing. The unit's account (held behaviour, not counted as evidence) is right, but before.log should say which run is the reference.

The measuring field and arms are gone: grep finds no price_open_cost / opencost in src, bench/src, bench/examples or tests. git status shows only the five intended files. vault::note costs one relaxed load and is reached only from open-only paths (manifest_read_all, on_device, open_refusals' cipher arm, unnamed_refusals, Wal::replay, whose sole caller is Db::open). No success path of a commit, sync, flush, drain, seal, rotation, publish or read changed.

A test with an unnamed run's or merge's segment whose last key only a seg- segment (store not yet partitioned) holds should be refused wrongly and go red. If nothing kills it, build that state.

manifest_read_all keeps files[i] only for a slot that parses (move `files[i] = Some(f)` after the parse succeeds). A torn other slot is then never synced. Expected killed by a_torn_publish_over_an_owed_slot_survives_a_power_cut_after_the_reopen (+cipher). Confirm.
N10 again, once the test records the synced descriptor: sync_slot given a File reopened by path (vault::open(path)) in place of slot_files[s].take(). Must die.

result.summary:
Repair round 1 fixed the one blocking finding. The test named for one open of each slot file, an_open_opens_each_slot_file_once (and its cipher twin), now checks which descriptor was used. Before, it only counted a trace record that a second open would not make. Now the slot read and the slot's fdatasync each record, through vault::note_file, the descriptor's number and its open file description's offset. The test asserts that each slot file was read whole through one descriptor and synced through that same (number, offset). Three forms of N10 now fail it: a reopen by path with the read's descriptor dropped, a reopen through vault::open, and a reopen with the read's descriptor still open.

Of the extra mutants, two survived at first:
- E1 (a seg- name takes no key). The new test an_open_after_a_crash_holds_an_unnamed_segments_keys_to_pieces_without_fences kills it: the store is not yet partitioned and the first merge is held at its landing.
- E8 (every pcs- name takes every key). The new test an_open_after_a_crash_reads_no_piece_whose_fences_leave_an_unnamed_segments_key_out kills it: pieces stand over the first and middle ranges, and the middle range's merge output ends at a key only a piece holds.

The rest:
- E2 (a slot's descriptor kept only when the slot parses) was killed by the torn-owed-slot tests. The brief listed it twice; it ran once.
- E5 (the runs' segments dropped from the candidates, routing kept) was killed.
- E4a, E4b, E7, E9 and E10 survive as expected. They change only cost (a linear search, on_disk in place of the listing, no break) or only which refusal answers first.

The unit's earlier work is kept:
- The slot handles manifest_read_all opened are the ones fdatasynced.
- In the clear, "is this segment there" is answered from one sorted listing; under a cipher vault::on_device still asks each envelope.
- One directory listing replaces three.
- unnamed_refusals runs before the log's replay.
- An unnamed segment's last key is looked up only in the candidates whose names' fences take it in, each mapped once, stopping at the first holder.

Pricing is unchanged from the unit's first pass. Folded against landed is level, and at 10000 keys clean and log the folded open is 1.5-2% faster in both sittings and both arms. Pricing was not re-run this round. The round adds no syscall, wait or allocation to an open with tracing off: a trace check moved after the slot read, and the sync's inline trace check became a call to the same check. No suite cell runs Db::open.

Durable 271, db 226, cipher 24, fuzz 5 and lib 406 all pass. clippy -D warnings and fmt --check are clean. The tree is byte for byte the kept copies in keep/*.fixed (sha256.txt).
result.shape_landed:
Db::open:
- manifest_read_all returns the slot Files it opened, and the open fdatasyncs both slots through those descriptors (vault::sync_slot). vault::open_slot_found is gone.
- One vault::names listing, sorted. In the clear, open_refusals answers with a binary search of it; under a cipher, vault::on_device per named envelope.
- The wal/spare loop and the runs' temp names read the same listing.
- unnamed_refusals runs right after open_refusals and before Wal::replay. It walks the candidates (the named segments, then the runs' segments beside a temp name), keeps those that Db::name_takes(name, last_key) by the fences in the name (a seg- name, or one that does not parse, takes every key), maps each once in a HashMap and stops at the first holder.
- Test-only trace records: vault::note (read_slot, on_device, open_holder, replay) and, new this round, vault::note_file / Db::trace_slot_descriptors, which record the descriptor number and offset for read_slot and sync_slot. Each costs one relaxed load when tracing is off.

result.summary:
Open-cost unit (followups 27, 38, 39, 57), as it stands after repair round 2. It is uncommitted in the tree, which matches keep/*.fixed byte for byte (checked against sha256.txt).

What it does to the open:
- Each manifest slot is fdatasynced through the descriptor manifest_read_all already opened, so the second open and close of each slot are gone.
- A plain store answers whether a named segment is there from its own sorted directory listing, by binary search. Under a cipher the per-envelope vault::on_device stat stays.
- The open's three directory listings are now one.
- unnamed_refusals runs before the log replay.
- To look up an unnamed segment's last key, the open maps only the named segments (and runs' segments) whose name fences take that key in (Db::name_takes), each mapped once. It stops at the first segment that holds the key.

Round 2 changed only tests/durable.rs; nothing under src/.
- I ran the reviewers' nine extra mutants as eight edits (two pairs were the same edit).
- X1 (`key < lo` became `key <= lo` in name_takes) survived the existing tests. I added an_open_after_a_crash_holds_an_unnamed_segments_key_at_its_ranges_lower_fence. It builds a partition holding only the key `m`, so its fence is the key itself. A piece rewrites `m`, the merge is held at its landing, and the store is copied there. The open must read a holder whose lower fence is the output's last key. The test passes on the fixed code and kills X1.
- Every other extra mutant was killed. The two skip mutants were expected to survive as cost-only; the routing trace tests kill them.
- X7 as written does not compile, because the loop uses slot_files. It was run as drop(std::mem::take(&mut slot_files)) ahead of the loop, and S3a's killers killed it.
- X8 is killed by the read's offset of 0 against the sync's offset of len, which confirms the offset holds the descriptor's identity, not the fd number.

Checks after the round: the durable, db, cipher, fuzz and lib suites are all green (272/226/24/5/406 passed). fmt.sh and clippy -D warnings both exit 0.

I did not re-run the pricing: the round changed no code under src/, and no reviewer showed that a pairing misses the mechanism.
result.shape_landed: The open fdatasyncs both slot files through the handles manifest_read_all opened, with no reopen. A plain store finds named segments by binary search of its single sorted listing; under a cipher vault::on_device stats each one. unnamed_refusals runs before the replay and maps only the candidates whose name fences take in the unnamed segment's last key, each once, stopping at the first that holds it. A seg- name, or a name with no parseable fences, takes every key. Trace notes are one relaxed load when tracing is off.

The tree was put back from keep/*.fixed with sha256 checked. A fresh `sh scripts/check.sh build test lint` then exited 0 ("all checks passed": cipher 24, durable 272, db 226, lib 406, clippy -D warnings, fmt check). This round changed no source and the extra-mutant list was empty, so there was no pricing re-run and no new mutants.
The unit as it stands:
- Each manifest slot is fdatasynced through the descriptor manifest_read_all read it through; vault::open_slot_found is gone.
- In the clear, one sorted directory listing answers whether each named segment is there (binary search). Under a cipher the per-envelope vault::on_device stat stays.
- The open's three listings are folded into one.
- unnamed_refusals runs before the log replay.
- An unnamed segment's last key is looked up only in the candidates whose name fences take it in (Db::name_takes). Each candidate is mapped once and the walk stops at the first holder.
The unit is uncommitted and byte for byte keep/*.fixed; the draft commit message is commit-msg.txt.
result.shape_landed: The open fdatasyncs both slot files through the File handles manifest_read_all opened (no second open or close). It takes one sorted directory listing, used for on_disk, the wal/spare loop and the runs' temp names. In the clear, open_refusals binary-searches that listing; under a cipher it calls vault::on_device per named envelope. unnamed_refusals runs right after open_refusals and before the replay. It routes the unnamed segment's last key only to the candidates whose par-/pcs- name fences [lo,hi) take it in (a seg- name, or one that does not parse, takes every key), maps each candidate once (HashMap) and breaks at the first holder. vault::note and vault::note_file are trace hooks for tests and cost one relaxed load when tracing is off. Db::trace_slot_descriptors is a #[doc(hidden)] seam.
